title.zh: 卷408 列傳一百九十五 李续宾 丁锐义 曾国华 李续宜 王珍弟：开化 刘腾鸿弟：腾鹤 蒋益澧
title.en: Volume 408 Biographies 195: Li Xubin, Ding Ruiyi, Ceng Guohua, Li Xuyi, Wang Zhen younger brother: Kai Hua, Liu Tenghong younger brother: Teng He, Jiang Yili
title.raw: 卷408 列傳一百九十五 李续宾 丁锐义 曾国华 李续宜 王珍弟：开化 刘腾鸿弟：腾鹤 蒋益澧

sentences.zh: =李續賓=李續賓，字迪庵，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Li Xubin, styled Di'an, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xubin, whose style was Di'an, came from Xiangxiang County in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 諸生，膂力過人，善騎射。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate; his physical strength surpassed others', and he was skilled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: A degree-holder, he possessed unusual strength and excelled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 羅澤南講學里中，折節受書。

translations.literal: Luo Zeren lectured in the locality, and he humbled himself to receive instruction in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Zeren taught in their home district, he set aside his pride to study under him.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，澤南募鄉勇殺賊，續賓奉父命往佐之，從平桂東土匪。

translations.literal: In the early Xianfeng period Zeren recruited local braves to kill rebels; Xubin, obeying his father's command, went to assist him and followed in pacifying the bandits of Guidong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign, when Zeren raised local militia to fight the rebels, Xubin's father sent him to serve under him, and he helped put down the Guidong bandits.

sentences.zh: 三年，援江西，令將右營。

translations.literal: In the third year he aided Jiangxi and was ordered to command the right battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he marched to aid Jiangxi and was placed in command of the right battalion.

sentences.zh: 澤南每戰，續賓皆從。

translations.literal: Whenever Zeren fought, Xubin always accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: Xubin accompanied Zeren on every campaign.

sentences.zh: 歸湖南，屯衡州，复永興。

translations.literal: He returned to Hunan, encamped at Hengzhou, and recovered Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: They returned to Hunan, encamped at Hengzhou, and retook Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，從澤南規岳州，湘軍僅千人，戰於大橋，續賓率數騎駐山岡，賊至不動，俟兵漸集，親搏戰，馳斬賊目，奪其旗，追北十餘​​里。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year, following Zeren in the plan against Yuezhou, the Hunan Army had only a thousand men; they fought at Daqiao Bridge; Xubin led several riders to hold a hill; when the rebels arrived he did not move; he waited until troops gradually gathered, then fought hand to hand himself, galloped and beheaded a rebel chieftain, seized their flag, and pursued north for more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: That summer of the fourth year, marching with Zeren against Yuezhou, the Hunan forces numbered barely a thousand. At the battle of Daqiao Bridge, Xubin took a few horsemen to a hillcrest and held his ground as the rebels approached. Once reinforcements had gathered, he joined the melee in person, rode down a rebel chief, captured the enemy standard, and drove the foe north for over ten li.

sentences.zh: 次日，塔齊布至戰地，服其勇，由是知名。

translations.literal: The next day Ta Qibu arrived at the battlefield, admired his bravery, and from this he became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ta Qibu came to the field, was impressed by his valor, and from then on Xubin was widely known.

sentences.zh: 連旬與賊戰，續賓曰：「賊不得擄掠，今且盡，可乘機薄其壘。」

translations.literal: For successive ten-day periods they fought the rebels; Xubin said: "The rebels cannot obtain plunder; they are now nearly exhausted; we may seize the opportunity to press close to their ramparts."
translations.idiomatic: After weeks of fighting the rebels, Xubin said, "They have been unable to forage for supplies and are nearly spent—we should take this chance to storm their stockade."

sentences.zh: 塔齊布從之。

translations.literal: Ta Qibu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Ta Qibu agreed.

sentences.zh: 會風雨，奮擊，連破賊壘，賊乃棄岳州而遁。

translations.literal: Wind and rain came; they struck fiercely, broke rebel ramparts in succession, and the rebels then abandoned Yuezhou and fled.
translations.idiomatic: A storm arose; they attacked with vigor, took one rebel fort after another, and the enemy abandoned Yuezhou and fled.

sentences.zh: 論功，累擢知縣。

translations.literal: In accounting merit he was repeatedly promoted to district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: For his merits he was promoted repeatedly, eventually to the rank of district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 從澤南克崇陽、咸寧，規武昌，大戰於花園，及破鮎魚套賊營，功皆最。

translations.literal: Following Zeren he captured Chongyang and Xianning, planned against Wuchang, fought a great battle at Huayuan, and when the Niuyutao rebel camp was broken his merit was foremost in all.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zeren in the capture of Chongyang and Xianning and the advance on Wuchang, fought a major battle at Huayuan, and led the charge in the storming of the Niuyutao camp—on every occasion his service ranked first.

sentences.zh: 武漢复，擢直隸州知州，賜花翎。

translations.literal: When Wuhan was recovered he was promoted to prefect of Zhili prefecture and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuhan was retaken he was raised to prefect of Zhizhou in Zhili and awarded the peacock plume.

sentences.zh: 進攻田家鎮，賊水陸數万，塔齊布阻於富池口，湘軍合寶勇僅二千六百人，咸色沮，續賓手刃逃者三人，軍心始固。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Tianjia Town, the rebels numbered tens of thousands on land and water; Ta Qibu was blocked at Fuchikou; the Hunan Army together with the Baoyong troops had only 2,600 men; all looked dispirited; Xubin personally executed three deserters with his blade, and the army's morale was then secured.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Tianjia Town the rebels mustered tens of thousands by land and water, while Ta Qibu was stalled at Fuchikou. The Hunan forces and the Baoyong contingent together numbered only 2,600, and spirits sank until Xubin cut down three runaways with his own hand; only then did the army steady itself.

sentences.zh: 大戰於半壁山，殺賊數千，焚其巢，遂平田家鎮。

translations.literal: They fought a great battle at Banbishan, killed several thousand rebels, burned their nest, and thereby pacified Tianjia Town.
translations.idiomatic: At Banbishan they fought a major engagement, killed thousands of rebels, burned their stronghold, and secured Tianjia Town.

sentences.zh: 擢知府，賜號摯勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect and granted the title Zhiyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefectural intendant and given the honorific title Resolute Brave Batulu.

sentences.zh: 尋授安慶知府。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed prefect of Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Anqing.

sentences.zh: 於是從羅澤南、塔齊布連复廣濟、黃梅，破賊於翟港、孔壟，每戰率為軍鋒。

translations.literal: Thereupon following Luo Zeren and Ta Qibu he successively recovered Guangji and Huangmei, defeated rebels at Zhaigang and Konglong, and in every battle invariably served as the army's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He then campaigned with Luo Zeren and Ta Qibu to retake Guangji and Huangmei, routed the rebels at Zhaigang and Konglong, and in battle after battle led the van.

sentences.zh: 進規九江，九江城堅，賊所聚合，攻不能下。

translations.literal: He advanced to plan against Jiujiang; Jiujiang's walls were strong and the rebels had gathered there; the attack could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: They moved against Jiujiang, whose walls were strong and where the rebels had massed, but the city could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 議分​​兵剿湖口、梅家洲，從澤南屯盔山。

translations.literal: It was proposed to divide troops to suppress Hukou and Meijiazhou; he followed Zeren in encamping at Kuishan.
translations.idiomatic: They decided to detach forces against Hukou and Meijiazhou while Xubin followed Zeren in encamping at Kuishan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，水師失利，入彭蠡湖，為賊所扼。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the naval forces suffered defeat, entered Poyang Lake, and were choked off by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the fleet was defeated and driven into Poyang Lake, where the rebels bottled it up.

sentences.zh: 續賓憤甚，請於曾國籓，自率千人渡江攻小池口，塔齊布率二十人偕行。

translations.literal: Xubin was deeply angered; he requested of Zeng Guofan to lead a thousand men himself across the river to attack Xiaochikou, and Ta Qibu led twenty men to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Xubin asked Zeng Guofan for permission to cross the Yangzi at the head of a thousand men and strike Xiaochikou; Ta Qibu went along with twenty followers.

sentences.zh: 塔齊布與續賓皆恃勇，每合戰，逼賊，席地坐，槍彈如雨，不顧，忽躍起突陣，橫厲無前，習以為常。

translations.literal: Ta Qibu and Xubin both relied on bravery; whenever they joined battle they pressed the rebels, sat on the ground, bullets fell like rain yet they paid no heed, then suddenly leaped up and burst into the formation, sweeping forward without peer—a thing they made habitual.
translations.idiomatic: Both Ta Qibu and Xubin were famed for daring: in every fight they pressed the enemy, would sit on the ground under a hail of musket fire without flinching, then spring up and charge the line, cutting through with reckless force until it became their custom.

sentences.zh: 至是眾寡懸絕，戰竟日不能克，暮收隊，而塔齊布失踪，欲再渡江入賊壘覓之，塔齊布旋自返。

translations.literal: On this occasion the disparity of numbers was extreme; they fought all day without victory; at evening they withdrew, and Ta Qibu was missing; Xubin wished again to cross the river and enter the rebel ramparts to seek him, but Ta Qibu soon returned on his own.
translations.idiomatic: This time they were hopelessly outnumbered; the fight lasted all day without success, and at dusk they drew off—only to find Ta Qibu missing. Xubin was ready to cross again and search the rebel lines, but Ta Qibu soon reappeared on his own.

sentences.zh: 五年春，粵匪由江寧大股上犯，武昌再陷。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year the Cantonese rebels in a great body from Jiangning advanced upward, and Wuchang fell again.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year a large Taiping force from Nanjing marched upriver and Wuchang fell once more.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓頓兵江西，續賓偕澤南從之。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan halted his army in Jiangxi, and Xubin accompanied Zeren in following him.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan held his forces in Jiangxi, and Xubin followed Zeren to join him.

sentences.zh: 尋分赴贛東攻剿，連复弋陽、廣信、德興、義寧，記名以道員用。

translations.literal: Soon they were detached to attack and suppress in eastern Gan, successively recovered Yiyang, Guangxin, Dexing, and Yining, and he was recorded by name for use as a circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: They were soon sent to campaign in eastern Jiangxi, retaking Yiyang, Guangxin, Dexing, and Yining in succession, and Xubin was placed on the rolls for appointment as a circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，回援湖北，克通城、崇陽，分兵趨羊樓峒。

translations.literal: That autumn they returned to aid Hubei, captured Tongcheng and Chongyang, and detached troops toward Yangloudong.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn they marched back to relieve Hubei, took Tongcheng and Chongyang, and sent a detachment toward Yangloudong.

sentences.zh: 策賊遠道赴援利速戰，堅守俟之。

translations.literal: He calculated that rebels coming from afar to aid would profit from a swift battle, and held firm in defense to await them.
translations.idiomatic: He reasoned that enemy reinforcements marching from a distance would want a quick fight, so he stood on the defensive and waited.

sentences.zh: 明日賊至，相持至暮，瞰其怠，突擊之，大潰。

translations.literal: The next day the rebels arrived; they faced off until evening; observing their slackness, he struck suddenly and they were routed in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came the next day; the standoff lasted until evening, when he saw them flagging, charged, and put them to rout.

sentences.zh: 蒲圻、咸寧相繼复，加鹽運使銜。

translations.literal: Puchi and Xianning were recovered in succession, and he was given the brevet rank of salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Puchi and Xianning were retaken in turn, and he received the brevet title of salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一月，進攻武昌，破塘角賊壘，又敗賊於窯灣，屢戰皆捷，蹋平城外賊壘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month they advanced on Wuchang, broke the Tangjiao rebel ramparts, again defeated rebels at Yaowan, won victory in repeated battles, and trampled flat the rebel ramparts outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they pressed the attack on Wuchang, stormed the Tangjiao forts, defeated the enemy again at Yaowan, won a string of victories, and leveled the rebel works outside the city.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，羅澤南以砲傷卒於軍，軍中新失帥，人情洶洶，賊復增壘抗拒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year Luo Zeren died in camp from a cannon wound; the army had newly lost its commander, morale was turbulent, and the rebels again added ramparts to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year Luo Zeren died of a gunshot wound in camp; with their commander gone the troops were unsettled, and the rebels threw up new works to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 巡撫胡林翼奏以續賓代領其眾，軍勢復振，盡剷平城外新壘，連於賽湖堤、小龜山、雙鳳山破城中出竄之賊。

translations.literal: Governor Hu Linyi memorialized that Xubin should replace him in command of his forces; the army's momentum revived; they completely leveled the new ramparts outside the walls and in succession at Saihudi, Xiaoguishan, and Shuangfengshan broke rebels sallying from the city.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Hu Linyi recommended that Xubin take command of Zeren's troops; the army rallied, cleared every new fort outside the walls, and repeatedly smashed rebel sorties at Saihudi, Xiaoguishan, and Shuangfengshan.

sentences.zh: 七月，石達開糾江南、江西各路賊七八萬來援，城賊將應之，續賓御之魯家港，旬日內大小二十餘戰，解散脅從萬餘，破賊二十餘壘，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Shi Dakai mustered seventy or eighty thousand rebels from all routes in Jiangnan and Jiangxi to come to the relief; the rebels in the city were about to respond; Xubin met them at Lujiagang; within ten days there were more than twenty great and small battles; he dispersed over ten thousand coerced followers and broke more than twenty rebel ramparts; he was given the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Shi Dakai gathered seventy or eighty thousand rebels from Jiangnan and Jiangxi to relieve the city; Xubin met them at Lujiagang and in ten days fought more than twenty engagements, disbanding over ten thousand pressed men and destroying more than twenty enemy camps, for which he received the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊閉城不出，乃開壕引江水灌入，為長圍困之。

translations.literal: The rebels shut the city and would not come out; he then opened trenches and led river water in to flood it, forming a long encirclement to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy refused to sally, he dug trenches and diverted the river to flood the city, tightening a long siege around it.

sentences.zh: 十一月，克武昌，記名以按察使用。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Wuchang was captured; he was recorded by name for use as provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang fell in the eleventh month, and he was placed on the rolls for appointment as provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 渡江克黃州，連復大冶、興國，直薄九江城下。

translations.literal: Crossing the river he captured Huangzhou, successively recovered Daye and Xingguo, and pressed straight to beneath the walls of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi, took Huangzhou, retook Daye and Xingguo in succession, and marched straight to the walls of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 九江賊首林啟榮堅守苦戰。

translations.literal: The Jiujiang rebel leader Lin Qirong held firm in bitter fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel commander at Jiujiang, Lin Qirong, defended the city in a desperate fight.

sentences.zh: 續賓復用攻武昌法，濬長壕三十里。

translations.literal: Xubin again employed the method used in attacking Wuchang and dug a long trench thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Xubin again used the siege method that had taken Wuchang and dug a trench encircling the city for thirty li.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，壕成，湖口、安慶賊迭來援，皆擊走之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year the trench was completed; rebels from Hukou and Anqing came in succession to relieve the city, and all were beaten off.
translations.idiomatic: By the third month of the seventh year the trench was finished; rebel relief columns from Hukou and Anqing came one after another, and each was driven off.

sentences.zh: 六月，賊犯蘄州、黃梅，續賓渡江迎擊於廣濟童司牌，大破之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month rebels invaded Qizhou and Huangmei; Xubin crossed the river to meet and attack them at Tongsipai in Guangji and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the rebels threatened Qizhou and Huangmei; Xubin crossed the river and crushed them at Tongsipai in Guangji.

sentences.zh: 合水師進攻小池口，毀其城。

translations.literal: Together with the naval forces he advanced to attack Xiaochikou and destroyed its walls.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the fleet in an assault on Xiaochikou and demolished the town.

sentences.zh: 策九江賊恃湖口為犄角，不拔湖口，九江不可得。

translations.literal: He calculated that the Jiujiang rebels relied on Hukou as a pincer position; without taking Hukou, Jiujiang could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: He judged that the Jiujiang garrison depended on Hukou as its flank; until Hukou fell, Jiujiang could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 九月，令弟續宜攻梅家洲，自率師揚言往宿松，潛伏湖口後山。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he ordered his younger brother Xuyi to attack Meijiazhou; he himself led troops, publicly announcing that they were going to Susong, but secretly lay in ambush on the hill behind Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he sent his brother Xuyi against Meijiazhou while he marched in the open toward Susong, then hid his main force on the ridge behind Hukou.

sentences.zh: 水師並至，分攻，賊方悉銳以拒。

translations.literal: The naval forces arrived together and attacked on separate fronts; the rebels then concentrated all their elite troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet joined the assault on several fronts, drawing the enemy's best troops into the fight.

sentences.zh: 續賓率士卒攀蘿至山椒，破空下，賊大駭，盡殲其眾。

translations.literal: Xubin led soldiers climbing vines to the mountain crest, broke through from above, the rebels were greatly terrified, and their entire force was annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Xubin led his men up the cliffs by the vines to the summit, then charged down from above; the rebels were thrown into panic and wiped out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 立克湖口縣城，梅家洲賊亦遁，乘勝克彭澤及小姑洑。

translations.literal: They immediately captured Hukou county seat; the Meijiazhou rebels also fled; riding the victory they captured Pengze and Xiaogufu.
translations.idiomatic: Hukou county fell at once; the Meijiazhou garrison fled, and the victors pressed on to take Pengze and Xiaogufu.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，授浙江布政使。

translations.literal: When the victory was reported he was appointed provincial administration commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: News of the victory brought his appointment as provincial administration commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 於是賊援遂絕。

translations.literal: Thereupon rebel reinforcements were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel relief was now cut off entirely.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，以地雷轟城百餘丈，梯而登，殄賊萬餘，擒林啟榮及李興隆等磔之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, using land mines they blasted more than a hundred zhang of wall, scaled ladders and mounted, exterminated more than ten thousand rebels, captured Lin Qirong and Li Xinglong and others and dismembered them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year a mine breach opened more than a hundred zhang of wall; his men went up the ladders, killed more than ten thousand defenders, and took Lin Qirong, Li Xinglong, and others, who were executed by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 九江平，加巡撫銜，賜黃馬褂，許專摺奏事。

translations.literal: Jiujiang was pacified; he was given the brevet rank of governor-general, granted the yellow riding jacket, and permitted memorials on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiujiang pacified he received the brevet rank of governor-general, the yellow riding jacket, and the right to submit memorials directly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 續賓既下九江，請假省親，抵湖北，陳玉成陷麻城、黃安，移兵擊走之。

translations.literal: After Xubin had taken Jiujiang he requested leave to visit his parents; reaching Hubei, Chen Yucheng had seized Macheng and Huang'an; he shifted troops and struck to drive him off.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiujiang fell Xubin asked leave to visit his family; on reaching Hubei he found Chen Yucheng had taken Macheng and Huang'an, and he marched to drive him off.

sentences.zh: 時續賓威望冠諸軍，浙人官京師者，合疏請飭援浙江。

translations.literal: At this time Xubin's prestige topped all armies; Zhejiang natives serving as officials in the capital jointly memorialized requesting that he be ordered to aid Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xubin's fame now stood above every other commander, and Zhejiang officials at court joined in a memorial asking that he be sent to relieve their province.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼議大舉進規安徽，詔將軍都興阿、總兵鮑超由宿松趨安慶，續賓由英山趨太湖。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi proposed a major advance to plan against Anhui; an edict ordered General Du Xing'a and Brigadier Bao Chao from Susong toward Anqing, and Xubin from Yingshan toward Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi urged a major offensive into Anhui; the court ordered General Du Xing'a and Brigadier Bao Chao from Susong toward Anqing and Xubin from Yingshan toward Taihu.

sentences.zh: 續賓乃留弟續宜屯武昌，自率八千人行，會起曾國籓視師，續賓復分所部千人與之，至太湖而署巡撫李孟群師潰廬州，改道赴援。

translations.literal: Xubin then left his younger brother Xuyi to garrison Wuchang and himself led eight thousand men on the march; it happened that Zeng Guofan was raised to inspect the army, and Xubin again detached a thousand men from his command to give him; reaching Taihu, Acting Governor Li Mengqun's army had been routed at Luzhou, and he changed route to go to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: Xubin left his brother Xuyi to hold Wuchang and marched with eight thousand men; when Zeng Guofan was appointed to oversee the armies, Xubin detached a thousand troops for him. At Taihu he learned that Acting Governor Li Mengqun's force had been shattered at Luzhou and turned aside to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 八月至九月，克楓香鋪、小池驛、梅心驛，复太湖、潛山、桐城、舒城，賊望風潰走。

translations.literal: From the eighth to the ninth month he captured Fengxiangpu, Xiaochiyi, and Meixinyi, recovered Taihu, Qianshan, Tongcheng, and Shucheng, and the rebels fled at the sight of the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Between the eighth and ninth months he took Fengxiangpu, Xiaochiyi, and Meixinyi and retook Taihu, Qianshan, Tongcheng, and Shucheng; the rebels broke and ran wherever he appeared.

sentences.zh: 軍無留行，進規廬州。

translations.literal: The army made no halt in its march and advanced to plan against Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The army did not pause and pressed on toward Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊於三河鎮築城，外列九壘，憑河設險，我軍非得三河不能進。

translations.literal: The rebels built a walled town at Sanhe Town, set nine ramparts outside, relied on the river to establish defenses, and our army could not advance without taking Sanhe.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fortified Sanhe Town and ringed it with nine outworks along the river; the Qing forces could not advance until Sanhe fell.

sentences.zh: 續賓克桐城、舒城後，各留守兵，所率臨敵僅五千人。

translations.literal: After Xubin captured Tongcheng and Shucheng he left garrison troops at each; those he led to face the enemy numbered only five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Tongcheng and Shucheng he left garrisons behind and went forward with only five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 十月，分三路攻賊，九壘皆下，殺賊七千餘，我軍傷亡亦逾千人。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he divided into three routes to attack the rebels; all nine ramparts were taken; more than seven thousand rebels were killed, and our army's casualties also exceeded a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he attacked on three fronts, carried all nine forts, killed more than seven thousand rebels, and lost over a thousand of his own men.

sentences.zh: 趣後軍未至，而陳玉成、李世賢糾合捻匪來援，眾十萬，連營十餘里。

translations.literal: He urged the rear army, which had not yet arrived, while Chen Yucheng and Li Shixian gathered Nian bandits to come to the relief, their force a hundred thousand, encamped in a continuous line for more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Before his reinforcements could come up, Chen Yucheng and Li Shixian rallied the Nian and other allies until a hundred thousand rebels were camped in a line more than ten li long.

sentences.zh: 諸將議退守桐城，續賓不可。

translations.literal: The generals discussed withdrawing to defend Tongcheng; Xubin would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged a retreat to Tongcheng, but Xubin refused.

sentences.zh: 夜半，部勒各營，旦日迎擊，至樊家渡，天大霧，賊分隊包抄，我軍驚潰，副將劉祜山，參將彭友勝，游擊胡廷槐、鄒玉堂、杜廷光，皆戰死。

translations.literal: At midnight he arrayed the various camps; at dawn he went out to meet the attack; reaching Fanjiadu, a great fog covered the sky; the rebels divided forces to envelop; our army panicked and collapsed; Vice Commander Liu Hushan, Staff Commander Peng Yousheng, and Mobile Corps Commanders Hu Tinghuai, Zou Yutang, and Du Tingguang all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he drew up the camps; at dawn he marched out to meet the enemy. At Fanjiadu a thick fog settled; rebel detachments swung around both flanks, the army broke in panic, and Vice Commander Liu Hushan, Staff Commander Peng Yousheng, and Mobile Corps Commanders Hu Tinghuai, Zou Yutang, and Du Tingguang were all killed.

sentences.zh: 續賓衝盪苦戰，賊集愈多，營壘皆破。

translations.literal: Xubin charged and fought bitterly; the rebels gathered ever more thickly, and the camps were all broken.
translations.idiomatic: Xubin fought on in the thick of it as the enemy closed in from every side and overran the camps.

sentences.zh: 或勸突圍出，圖再振，續賓曰：「軍興十年，皆以退走損國威。

translations.literal: Some urged him to break out and escape, planning to rally again; Xubin said: "In ten years since the armies were raised, every retreat has damaged the state's prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to break out and fight another day; Xubin said, "For ten years of war every retreat has cost the dynasty its prestige.

sentences.zh: 吾前後數百戰，出隊即不望生還。

translations.literal: In my hundreds of battles before and after, whenever I went out with the column I did not expect to return alive.
translations.idiomatic: In hundreds of battles I have never marched out expecting to come back alive.

sentences.zh: 今日必死，不原從者自為計。」

translations.literal: Today I must die; those who do not wish to follow may make their own plans."
translations.idiomatic: Today I shall die; whoever does not wish to follow me may save himself."

sentences.zh: 諸將士皆曰：「原從公死！」

translations.literal: All the officers and soldiers said: "We wish to follow you in death!"
translations.idiomatic: His officers and men cried, "We will die with you!"

sentences.zh: 日暮上馬，開壁擊殺數百人。

translations.literal: At dusk he mounted his horse, opened the rampart, and struck, killing several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he mounted, threw open the stockade, and cut down several hundred of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 總兵李續燾、副將彭祥瑞越壘衝出，賊踞其壘，決河堤，斷去路。

translations.literal: Brigadier Li Xudan and Vice Commander Peng Xiangrui crossed the rampart and broke out; the rebels occupied their camp, breached the river dike, and cut off the road of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Brigadier Li Xudan and Vice Commander Peng Xiangrui broke out over the wall, but the rebels seized the camp, breached the river dike, and cut off the escape route.

sentences.zh: 續賓具衣冠望闕叩首，取所奉廷旨及批摺焚之，曰：「不可使宸翰污賊手。」

translations.literal: Xubin donned full dress, faced the palace and kowtowed, took the court edicts and annotated memorials he had received and burned them, saying: "The imperial brush must not be defiled by rebel hands."
translations.idiomatic: Xubin put on his full dress, bowed toward the palace, and burned the edicts and annotated memorials he carried, saying, "The emperor's writing must not fall into rebel hands."

sentences.zh: 躍馬馳入賊陣，死之。

translations.literal: He leaped on his horse and galloped into the rebel formation and died.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred his horse into the enemy ranks and was killed.

sentences.zh: 同知曾國華，知府何忠駿，知州王揆一，同知董容方，知縣楊德訚，從九品李續蓺、張溥萬，皆殉焉。

translations.literal: Subprefect Zeng Guohua, prefect He Zhongjun, prefect Wang Kuiyi, subprefect Dong Rongfang, magistrate Yang Deyin, and ninth-rank subofficials Li Xuyi and Zhang Puwan all died with him.
translations.idiomatic: Subprefect Zeng Guohua, Prefect He Zhongjun, Prefect Wang Kuiyi, Subprefect Dong Rongfang, Magistrate Yang Deyin, and subofficials Li Xuyi and Zhang Puwan all perished with him.

sentences.zh: 道員孫守信、運同丁銳義猶守中右營，越三日營陷，同死之。

translations.literal: Circuit intendant Sun Shouxin and transport subcommissioner Ding Ruiyi still held the central right battalion; after three days the camp fell and they died together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit intendant Sun Shouxin and transport subcommissioner Ding Ruiyi still held the central right battalion; three days later the camp was overrun and they died with him.

sentences.zh: 是役文武官弁死者數百人，士卒數千人。

translations.literal: In this battle several hundred civil and military officers died, and several thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In that battle several hundred officers and several thousand soldiers were killed.

sentences.zh: 時方有旨命會辦安徽軍務，及死事上聞，文宗流涕，手敕曰：「惜我良將，不克令終。

translations.literal: At this time there had just been an edict appointing him to assist in Anhui military affairs; when news of his death reached the throne, Emperor Wenzong wept and wrote in his own hand: "Alas for my fine general, who could not be granted a peaceful end.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had just appointed him to assist in Anhui; when word of his death reached the court, Emperor Wenzong wept and wrote in his own hand, "Alas for my fine general, denied a peaceful end.

sentences.zh: 尚冀忠靈不昧，他年生申、甫以佐予也！」

translations.literal: I still hope his loyal spirit is not dimmed, and that another Shen or Fu may be born in later days to assist me!"
translations.idiomatic: May his loyal spirit endure, and may Heaven one day send another Shen Bo or Fu Shang to aid me!"

sentences.zh: 贈總督，入祀昭忠祠，立功地建專祠，諡忠武。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the rank of governor-general, entered for worship in the Shrine of Loyalty and Fidelity, a special shrine was built at the place of his merit, and he was given the posthumous title Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made governor-general, enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty and Fidelity, granted a private temple at the scene of his service, and given the posthumous name Zhongwu (Loyal and Martial).

sentences.zh: 賜其父一品封典，子光久、光令並賜舉人，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: His father was granted a first-rank ennoblement patent; his sons Guangjiu and Guangling were both granted licentiate status; he was given the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father received a first-rank ennoblement, his sons Guangjiu and Guangling were both granted the juren degree by imperial favor, and the family received the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 續賓既歿，曾國籓疏上其生平戰績，略曰：「續賓隨羅澤南征剿，循循不自表異。

translations.literal: After Xubin had died Zeng Guofan memorialized his life's battles, saying in summary: "Xubin followed Luo Zeren in campaigning and suppressing rebels, proceeding step by step without displaying himself as exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: After Xubin's death Zeng Guofan submitted a memorial on his career, writing in part: "Xubin campaigned under Luo Zeren with steady modesty and never put himself forward.

sentences.zh: 岳州之戰，所將白旗，號為無敵，田家鎮以少勝眾。

translations.literal: In the battle of Yuezhou the white-banner troops he commanded were called invincible; at Tianjia Town he defeated the many with the few.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuezhou his white-banner battalion was called invincible; at Tianjia Town he beat a larger force with fewer men.

sentences.zh: 九江之敗，士卒多逃，獨所部依依不去，眾稱其能得士心。

translations.literal: In the defeat at Jiujiang many soldiers fled, but only his own troops clung to him and would not leave; all praised his ability to win men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiujiang was lost many men ran, but his own troops would not leave him, and men said he alone knew how to hold an army's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 軍中人人以氣節相高，獨默然深藏。

translations.literal: In the army everyone prized moral integrity, yet he alone remained silent and kept it hidden.
translations.idiomatic: In camp every man made a show of high principle, but he kept his own counsel.

sentences.zh: 然忠果之色，見​​於眉宇。

translations.literal: Yet the color of loyalty and resolution showed in his brows and eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Still, loyalty and resolve showed plainly in his face.

sentences.zh: 遠近上下，皆信其大節不苟。

translations.literal: Near and far, high and low, all trusted that his great integrity was unbending.
translations.idiomatic: Men high and low, near and far, all believed his integrity was absolute.

sentences.zh: 臣所立湘勇營製，行之既久，各營時有變更，獨續賓守法，始終不變。

translations.literal: The Hunan brave battalion regulations I established had been in force a long time; the various camps from time to time made changes, but Xubin alone kept the law and never altered it from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: The Hunan militia regulations I drew up had long been in use, and other camps often bent them, but Xubin alone held to the rules without change.

sentences.zh: 歷年節省餉項及廉俸，不寄家自肥，概留備軍中非常之需。

translations.literal: Over the years he saved from pay allotments and his integrity salary, did not send money home to enrich himself, and kept it all in reserve for the army's extraordinary needs.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year he saved from rations and his official salary, sent nothing home for his own gain, and kept it all for the army's emergencies.

sentences.zh: 量力濟人，不忍他軍飢而己軍獨飽。

translations.literal: According to his strength he aided others; he could not bear that other armies should hunger while his own alone was full.
translations.idiomatic: He shared what he could and could not bear to see other units go hungry while his men ate their fill.

sentences.zh: 馭下極寬，而弁勇有罪，往往揮淚手刃之。

translations.literal: In commanding subordinates he was extremely lenient, yet when officers and braves were guilty he often wept as he personally executed them with his blade.
translations.idiomatic: He was very easy on his men, yet when an officer or soldier deserved death he often killed him with his own hand, weeping as he did so.

sentences.zh: 至於臨陣，專以救敗為務。

translations.literal: As for facing battle, he made rescuing defeat his sole task.
translations.idiomatic: In battle his one concern was to retrieve a lost fight.

sentences.zh: 遇賊則讓人御其弱者，自當其悍者。

translations.literal: When he met rebels he let others face the weak while he himself took on the fierce.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy appeared he left the weaker foes to others and took the toughest himself.

sentences.zh: 分兵則以強者予人，而攜弱者自隨。

translations.literal: When dividing troops he gave the strong to others and kept the weak with himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he detached units he gave others his best men and kept the raw recruits with him.

sentences.zh: 弱者漸強，又易新營。

translations.literal: When the weak gradually grew strong, he again exchanged them for new camps.
translations.idiomatic: Once the weak had hardened into veterans, he took on a fresh batch of green troops.

sentences.zh: 軍中每言肯攜帶弱兵，肯臨陣救人者，前惟塔齊布，後惟續賓。

translations.literal: In the army they often said that those willing to take weak soldiers along and willing to save men in battle were, before only Ta Qibu, and afterward only Xubin.
translations.idiomatic: Camp talk had it that only Ta Qibu before him, and only Xubin after, would march with weak troops and risk himself to rescue others in a fight.

sentences.zh: 三河之敗，亦由分兵所致。

translations.literal: The defeat at Sanhe also arose from dividing troops.
translations.idiomatic: The disaster at Sanhe, too, came of his habit of splitting his force.

sentences.zh: 此軍民所由感泣不忘者也。」

translations.literal: This is why soldiers and civilians alike were moved to tears and could not forget him."
translations.idiomatic: This is why soldiers and civilians wept for him and would not forget him."

sentences.zh: 於是特詔嘉其有古名將風，以國籓疏宣付史館，用示褒異。

translations.literal: Thereupon a special edict praised him as having the manner of the ancient famous generals; Guofan's memorial was proclaimed and sent to the Historiographical Office to show exceptional commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then issued a special edict praising his ancient general's spirit, ordered Zeng's memorial published, and sent it to the Historiographical Office as a mark of exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 洎江南平，軫念前勞，加二等輕車都尉，並為男爵，子光久襲。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, remembering his former labors, he was given a second-class Commandant of Light Chariots and concurrently made a baron; his son Guangjiu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: After the south was pacified the court remembered his service, raised his hereditary rank to second-class Commandant of Light Chariots, made him a baron, and his son Guangjiu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: =丁銳義=丁銳義，字伯冕，長沙人。

translations.literal: Ding Ruiyi, styled Bomi, was a native of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Ruiyi, whose style was Bomi, came from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 治鄉團有聲，咸豐四年，從胡林翼援湖北，募壯士百人，後增至千人，號義字營。

translations.literal: In organizing local militia he had a reputation; in the fourth year of Xianfeng he followed Hu Linyi to aid Hubei, recruited a hundred stalwarts, later increased to a thousand, called the Yizi Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: He won fame organizing local militia; in the fourth year of Xianfeng he followed Hu Linyi to Hubei, raised a hundred men, later a thousand, known as the Yizi Battalion.

sentences.zh: 戰武漢，以勇聞。

translations.literal: Fighting at Wuhan, he became known for bravery.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Wuhan and earned a name for courage.

sentences.zh: 六年，羅澤南傷殞，賊酋古隆賢率眾犯官軍後路。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Luo Zeren died of wounds; the rebel chieftain Gu Longxian led a host to attack the government army's rear.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, after Luo Zeren was killed, the rebel leader Gu Longxian struck at the army's rear.

sentences.zh: 諸將以新失帥，皆主堅守。

translations.literal: The generals, having newly lost their commander, all advocated holding firm in defense.
translations.idiomatic: With their commander just dead, the other generals all favored staying on the defensive.

sentences.zh: 銳義曰：「我軍頓城下六閱月，求戰不得。

translations.literal: Ruiyi said: "Our army has halted beneath the walls for six months and could not obtain battle.
translations.idiomatic: Ruiyi said, "We have sat before these walls for six months without a fight.

sentences.zh: 今賊來乘我，出其不意，可一鼓滅。」

translations.literal: Now the rebels come to take advantage of us; if we catch them unawares we can destroy them in one drumbeat."
translations.idiomatic: Now they come to catch us off guard—we can crush them in a single stroke."

sentences.zh: 林翼壯之，令與唐訓方、蔣益澧、孫守信等夜出掩擊，大破賊於豹子海。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi was heartened by this and ordered him with Tang Xunfang, Jiang Yili, Sun Shouxin, and others to go out by night in a surprise attack, routing the rebels greatly at Baozihai.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi approved; that night Ruiyi joined Tang Xunfang, Jiang Yili, Sun Shouxin, and others in a surprise attack and routed the enemy at Baozihai.

sentences.zh: 又戰葛店、華容，奪樊口賊舟，克武昌縣，圍黃州。

translations.literal: He again fought at Gedian and Huarong, seized rebel boats at Fankou, captured Wuchang county, and besieged Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Gedian and Huarong, seized rebel boats at Fankou, took Wuchang county, and besieged Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會大水，退軍屯青山。

translations.literal: Great floods came; the army withdrew and encamped at Qingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Floods forced a withdrawal to encamp at Qingshan.

sentences.zh: 武漢复，擢知縣。

translations.literal: When Wuhan was recovered he was promoted to district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuhan was retaken he was promoted to district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 駐防蘄、黃間，屢與鄉團卻敵。

translations.literal: Garrisoning between Qizhou and Huangzhou, he repeatedly with local militia repelled the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Stationed between Qizhou and Huangzhou, he repeatedly drove off the enemy with local militia.

sentences.zh: 八年，破黃泥畈、青天畈賊壘，擢同知。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he broke the rebel ramparts at Huangnifan and Qingtianfan and was promoted to subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he stormed the forts at Huangnifan and Qingtianfan and was raised to subprefect.

sentences.zh: 又破賊於南陽河、阿彌鎮，擢運同。

translations.literal: He again defeated rebels at Nanyang River and Amizhen and was promoted to transport subcommissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the rebels again at Nanyang River and Amizhen and was made transport subcommissioner.

sentences.zh: 遂從李續賓進剿安徽，破石牌賊壘，連下數縣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed Li Xubin in advancing to suppress Anhui, broke the Shipai rebel ramparts, and in succession took several counties.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Li Xubin into Anhui, stormed the Shipai forts, and took several counties in succession.

sentences.zh: 將進攻三河，銳義諫曰：「孤軍深入，留兵四城，分力之半，死傷復多，士罷將驕，賊援將集，而貪進不已，此所謂強弩之末也。

translations.literal: About to advance on Sanhe, Ruiyi remonstrated: "A lone army penetrating deep, leaving troops in four cities, dividing strength by half, casualties again many, soldiers weary and generals arrogant, rebel relief about to gather, yet greedily advancing without cease—this is what is called the end of a strong crossbow.
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to attack Sanhe, Ruiyi warned, "We have marched deep with a single column, left men in four towns, and halved our strength; casualties mount, the men are tired and the officers overconfident, and enemy reinforcements are gathering—yet we press on. This is the last force of a spent bow.

sentences.zh: 使賊斷絕我餉道，舒、桐、潛、太兵少，見勝則怠，見敗必潰，四城將並覆。

translations.literal: If the rebels cut off our supply route, Shucheng, Tongcheng, Qianshan, and Taihu have few troops; seeing victory they grow slack, seeing defeat they will surely collapse, and the four cities will all be overthrown together.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy cuts our supply line, the garrisons at Shucheng, Tongcheng, Qianshan, and Taihu are too weak—they will slacken after a win and break after a loss, and all four towns will fall.

sentences.zh: 乃令退師桐城，休息待援，僅可不敗耳。」

translations.literal: Therefore order the army to withdraw to Tongcheng, rest and await relief—only thus may we avoid defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw to Tongcheng, rest, and wait for reinforcements—that is the only way to avoid disaster."

sentences.zh: 續賓不聽，銳義乃馳書湖北請援。

translations.literal: Xubin would not listen; Ruiyi then sent a rapid dispatch to Hubei requesting relief.
translations.idiomatic: Xubin would not hear of it, and Ruiyi sent an urgent plea to Hubei for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 續賓讓之曰：「君嘗以千人破賊數万，乃何怯耶！」

translations.literal: Xubin reproached him, saying: "You once with a thousand men broke tens of thousands of rebels—why so timid now!"
translations.idiomatic: Xubin rebuked him: "You once routed tens of thousands with a thousand men—what makes you timid now?"

sentences.zh: 及續賓軍敗，銳義率所部急救，身被數創。

translations.literal: When Xubin's army was defeated, Ruiyi led his own troops in urgent rescue and himself received several wounds.
translations.idiomatic: When Xubin's army was beaten, Ruiyi rushed to the rescue with his own men and was wounded several times.

sentences.zh: 續賓突圍戰死，銳義偕孫守信堅守其壁。

translations.literal: Xubin broke out and died in battle; Ruiyi together with Sun Shouxin held firm in his rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Xubin broke out and was killed; Ruiyi and Sun Shouxin held the stockade.

sentences.zh: 三日壘破，死之。

translations.literal: After three days the rampart was broken and they died.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the fort fell and they died with it.

sentences.zh: 銳義耳聾，喜論兵，戰每孤軍勇進。

translations.literal: Ruiyi was deaf, delighted in discussing military affairs, and in battle always advanced alone with a brave force.
translations.idiomatic: Ruiyi was deaf, loved to talk strategy, and in battle often charged ahead with a lone detachment.

sentences.zh: 獨三河之役主持重，而說不見用。

translations.literal: Only at Sanhe did he hold weighty views, yet his counsel was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At Sanhe alone his counsel carried weight, and it went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 卹贈鹽運使，加太常寺卿、騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: Posthumous gifts granted him salt transport commissioner, with addition of Grand Master of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and hereditary Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made salt transport commissioner, with the added ranks of Grand Master of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and hereditary Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 孫守信，亦長沙人。

translations.literal: Sun Shouxin was also a native of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shouxin, too, was from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 由內閣供事敘從九品，官湖北，從軍積功，累擢道員。

translations.literal: Through service in the Grand Secretariat he was ranked ninth-rank subofficial; he served in Hubei, followed the army accumulating merit, and was repeatedly promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from a ninth-rank clerk in the Grand Secretariat to office in Hubei, campaigned with the army, and was promoted repeatedly to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 未嘗獨將，與銳義為友，臨危不去。

translations.literal: He had never commanded alone; he was friends with Ruiyi and would not leave in peril.
translations.idiomatic: He had never held independent command; he was Ruiyi's friend and would not abandon him in danger.

sentences.zh: 同及於難。

translations.literal: Together they met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He perished in the same disaster.

sentences.zh: 贈按察使，加太常寺卿、騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted provincial surveillance commissioner, with addition of Grand Master of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and hereditary Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made provincial surveillance commissioner, with the added ranks of Grand Master of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and hereditary Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: =曾國華=曾國華，字溫甫，國籓弟。

translations.literal: Zeng Guohua, styled Wenfu, was Guofan's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guohua, whose style was Wenfu, was the younger brother of Zeng Guofan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，國籓兵困於江西，國華請於父，赴湖北乞師。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng Guofan's army was trapped in Jiangxi; Guohua asked his father and went to Hubei to beg for troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianfeng, with Guofan's army trapped in Jiangxi, Guohua asked his father's leave and went to Hubei to raise reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼令劉騰鴻，吳坤修、普承堯率五千人往援，以國華領其軍。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi ordered Liu Tenghong, Wu Kunxiu, and Pu Chengyao to lead five thousand men to the relief, with Guohua placed in command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi sent Liu Tenghong, Wu Kunxiu, and Pu Chengyao with five thousand men to relieve him, with Guohua in overall command.

sentences.zh: 攻克咸寧、蒲圻、通城、新昌、上高，以達瑞州。

translations.literal: He captured Xianning, Puchi, Tongcheng, Xinchang, and Shanggao, reaching Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: They took Xianning, Puchi, Tongcheng, Xinchang, and Shanggao on the march to Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 騰鴻戰城南，國華偕承堯戰城西北，屢破賊。

translations.literal: Tenghong fought south of the city; Guohua together with Chengyao fought northwest of the city and repeatedly defeated rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Tenghong fought south of the city while Guohua and Chengyao fought in the northwest and repeatedly routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 國籓至，乃合圍，掘塹周三十里，斷賊接濟。

translations.literal: When Guofan arrived they then combined in encirclement, dug trenches for thirty li around, and cut off rebel supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When Guofan arrived they closed the ring, dug a thirty-li trench, and cut the enemy's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 會丁父憂，偕國籓奔喪去軍。

translations.literal: It happened that his father died; together with Guofan he left the army to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When their father died, he and Guofan left the army for mourning.

sentences.zh: 與李續賓姻家，招佐軍事。

translations.literal: He was related by marriage to Li Xubin and was recruited to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Related by marriage to Li Xubin, he was invited to serve on his staff.

sentences.zh: 當連克四縣，軍勢銳甚，國華以常勝軍家所忌，時與續賓深語，並書告國籓。

translations.literal: When four counties were taken in succession the army's momentum was very sharp; Guohua, because a perpetually victorious army is what families fear, often spoke deeply with Xubin and also wrote to inform Guofan.
translations.idiomatic: After four counties fell in a row the army was at its peak; knowing that constant victory breeds envy, Guohua often spoke frankly with Xubin and wrote to Guofan as well.

sentences.zh: 及軍敗，從續賓力戰死，贈道銜，予騎都尉世職，諡愍烈。

translations.literal: When the army was defeated he followed Xubin fighting fiercely and died; he was posthumously granted circuit rank, given hereditary Commandant of Cavalry, and given the posthumous title Minlie.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was destroyed he fought beside Xubin to the death; he was posthumously given circuit rank, the hereditary Commandant of Cavalry, and the posthumous name Minlie (Sorrowful and Fierce).

sentences.zh: =李續宜=李續宜，字希庵，續賓弟。

translations.literal: Li Xuyi, styled Xi'an, was Xubin's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuyi, whose style was Xi'an, was Li Xubin's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 同事羅澤南。

translations.literal: He studied under Luo Zeren together with his brother.
translations.idiomatic: He had studied under Luo Zeren with his brother.

sentences.zh: 以文童從軍，援江西、湖北，積功累擢同知，賜花翎。

translations.literal: As a literary youth he followed the army, aided Jiangxi and Hubei, accumulated merit and was repeatedly promoted to subprefect, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the army as a young scholar, served in Jiangxi and Hubei, rose through repeated promotions to subprefect, and received the peacock plume.

sentences.zh: 武昌、漢陽复，胡林翼疏陳續宜功多為續賓所掩，詔以知府選用。

translations.literal: When Wuchang and Hanyang were recovered, Hu Linyi memorialized that much of Xuyi's merit had been overshadowed by Xubin; an edict ordered his selection as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuchang and Hanyang were retaken, Hu Linyi reported that much of Xuyi's merit had been credited to Xubin; the court ordered him selected for appointment as prefect.

sentences.zh: 從續賓攻九江，賊由安徽上犯蘄、黃以牽我師。

translations.literal: Following Xubin in attacking Jiujiang, rebels from Anhui advanced upward against Qizhou and Huangzhou to pin down our army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xubin against Jiujiang; rebels from Anhui struck Qizhou and Huangzhou to pin down the Qing forces.

sentences.zh: 咸豐七年，續宜率兵千七百人回援湖北，戰於黃州壩崎山，分三路進，毀賊壘，次蘄水、黃岡界。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xianfeng Xuyi led 1,700 troops back to aid Hubei, fought at Baqishan in Huangzhou, advanced on three routes, destroyed rebel ramparts, and next reached the border of Qishui and Huanggang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xianfeng Xuyi led 1,700 men back to Hubei, fought at Baqishan in Huangzhou on three fronts, destroyed enemy forts, and pushed to the Qishui–Huanggang border.

sentences.zh: 上馬家河、火石港、郴柳灣賊壘林立，傾巢出撲，續宜伏兵山下，驟起突擊，賊大亂，譟，乘之，破壘四十，移屯蘄水。

translations.literal: At Majiahe, Huoshigang, and Chenliuwang rebel ramparts stood in dense array; they came out in full force to strike; Xuyi hid troops below the hill, suddenly rose in a surprise attack, the rebels were in great disorder and clamor; he rode the momentum, broke forty ramparts, and moved camp to Qishui.
translations.idiomatic: At Majiahe, Huoshigang, and Chenliuwang the rebels had fortified in depth and came out in force; Xuyi hid men below the hill, sprang the ambush, threw them into chaos, and pressed the attack, taking forty forts before moving camp to Qishui.

sentences.zh: 遇援賊於月山，誘至山角，發砲擊之，潰，直搗其巢，焚屯聚數十處，破偽城五。

translations.literal: Meeting relief rebels at Yueshan, he lured them to a mountain corner, opened cannon fire on them, they collapsed, he struck straight at their nest, burned several dozen encampments, and broke five false cities.
translations.idiomatic: At Yueshan he lured enemy reinforcements into a corner of the hills, shelled them into flight, stormed their base, burned dozens of camps, and took five rebel strongholds.

sentences.zh: 會克小池口，以道員用，賜號伊勒達巴圖魯，由是續宜之名與其兄相頡頏。

translations.literal: When Xiaochikou was captured he was used as circuit intendant and granted the title Yileda Batulu; from this Xuyi's name rivaled his elder brother's.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaochikou fell he was placed on the rolls as circuit intendant and given the title Yileda Batulu; from then on his fame matched his brother's.

sentences.zh: 回軍江西，會攻梅家洲，克湖口。

translations.literal: Returning the army to Jiangxi, he joined in attacking Meijiazhou and captured Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Jiangxi, joined the attack on Meijiazhou, and took Hukou.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊酋韋俊率眾二萬复犯湖口。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the rebel chieftain Wei Jun led twenty thousand men again to invade Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the rebel commander Wei Jun returned with twenty thousand men to retake Hukou.

sentences.zh: 續宜駐蝘蚘山，分兵三路，一出馬影橋，一出流澌橋，一扼勞家渡，賊來，擊卻之。

translations.literal: Xuyi encamped at Yanshan, divided troops on three routes—one out from Maying Bridge, one from Liushi Bridge, one blocking Laojiadu—and when rebels came he beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: Xuyi held Yanshan and divided his force: one column at Maying Bridge, one at Liushi Bridge, one blocking Laojiadu; each enemy attack was repulsed.

sentences.zh: 而賊由西洋橋、排龍口、二賢寺直趨蝘蚘山，續宜麾諸路奮擊，斬獲千餘。

translations.literal: But rebels from Xiyang Bridge, Pailongkou, and Erxian Temple pressed straight toward Yanshan; Xuyi commanded all routes to strike fiercely and killed or captured more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels then advanced from Xiyang Bridge, Pailongkou, and Erxian Temple straight on Yanshan; Xuyi ordered every column forward and killed or captured more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 馳抵磨盤山，設伏破泰坪關援賊，賊乃遁。

translations.literal: He galloped to Mopanshan, set an ambush and broke the Taipingguan relief rebels, and the rebels then fled.
translations.idiomatic: He raced to Mopanshan, ambushed and broke the relief column from Taipingguan, and the enemy fled.

sentences.zh: 八年，九江既克，陳玉成由安徽竄蘄、黃，陷黃安。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, after Jiujiang was captured, Chen Yucheng fled from Anhui into Qizhou and Huangzhou and seized Huang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after Jiujiang fell, Chen Yucheng slipped from Anhui into Qizhou and Huangzhou and took Huang'an.

sentences.zh: 續宜馳援不利，續賓繼至，合擊。

translations.literal: Xuyi galloped to the relief without success; Xubin followed and they joined in attack.
translations.idiomatic: Xuyi's rushed relief failed until Xubin arrived and they attacked together.

sentences.zh: 續宜攻北門，破其壘，賊夜遁，复黃安。

translations.literal: Xuyi attacked the north gate, broke their ramparts, the rebels fled by night, and Huang'an was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Xuyi stormed the north gate, broke the works, and the enemy fled by night; Huang'an was retaken.

sentences.zh: 進至麻城，賊不戰引去。

translations.literal: Advancing to Macheng, the rebels withdrew without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: At Macheng the rebels withdrew without a fight.

sentences.zh: 續賓出師規安徽，胡林翼疏請留續宜固楚疆。

translations.literal: Xubin marched out to plan against Anhui; Hu Linyi memorialized requesting that Xuyi be kept to secure the Chu frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Xubin marched into Anhui, Hu Linyi asked that Xuyi be left to hold Hubei.

sentences.zh: 洎三河師熸，續賓戰歿，續宜在黃州，收輯殘部，思鄉者遣歸，原留者歸伍，差汰罪將，簡用其良，申儆訓練，經歲軍氣始復振。

translations.literal: When the Sanhe army was destroyed and Xubin died in battle, Xuyi was at Huangzhou; he gathered the remnants, sent home those who longed for their villages, returned to the ranks those who wished to stay, removed guilty generals, selected the good, issued warnings and training, and after a year the army's spirit began to revive.
translations.idiomatic: After the disaster at Sanhe and Xubin's death, Xuyi was at Huangzhou; he gathered the survivors, sent the homesick home, kept those who wished to stay, cashiered guilty officers, promoted the able, tightened discipline, and within a year the army's morale returned.

sentences.zh: 九年，授荊宜施道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed circuit intendant of Jing-Yi-Shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made circuit intendant of Jing-Yi-Shi.

sentences.zh: 石達開由江西竄入湖南，眾號三十萬，圍寶慶府城。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai fled from Jiangxi into Hunan, his force claiming three hundred thousand, and besieged Baoqing prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai broke from Jiangxi into Hunan with a host said to number three hundred thousand and besieged Baoqing.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼檄續宜率兵五千馳援，諸援軍悉歸統屬。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi ordered Xuyi to lead five thousand troops in rapid relief; all relief armies were placed under his unified command.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi ordered Xuyi to the relief with five thousand men and placed every other relief column under his command.

sentences.zh: 時援軍三萬餘，城被圍兩月。

translations.literal: At this time relief troops numbered more than thirty thousand; the city had been besieged two months.
translations.idiomatic: Relief forces now numbered more than thirty thousand; the city had been under siege for two months.

sentences.zh: 賊眾，食且盡，野掠無所得，聞續宜至，攻愈急。

translations.literal: The rebels were numerous, food was nearly exhausted, plunder in the countryside yielded nothing; hearing Xuyi had arrived, they attacked ever more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were many, their food nearly gone, and foraging yielded nothing; when word came that Xuyi was near, they pressed the assault all the harder.

sentences.zh: 續宜渡資江而軍，與劉長佑軍當賊衝，四戰而圍解，賊竄廣西境。

translations.literal: Xuyi crossed the Zi River and encamped, with Liu Changyou's army facing the rebels' thrust; after four battles the siege was lifted and the rebels fled into Guangxi territory.
translations.idiomatic: Xuyi crossed the Zi River and, with Liu Changyou's force blocking the enemy's main thrust, fought four engagements, lifted the siege, and drove the rebels into Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉續宜赴援迅速，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: An edict praised Xuyi's rapid march to the relief and added the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his swift march to the relief and gave him the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷安徽按察使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Anhui provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to provincial surveillance commissioner of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 曾國荃方圍安慶，多隆阿攻桐城，續宜率萬人屯青草塥，在安慶、桐城之間。

translations.literal: Zeng Guoquan was then besieging Anqing and Duo Long'a attacking Tongcheng; Xuyi led ten thousand men to encamp at Qingcaogai, between Anqing and Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: While Zeng Guoquan besieged Anqing and Duo Long'a attacked Tongcheng, Xuyi encamped ten thousand men at Qingcaogai between the two cities.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成以十萬眾來援，續宜與多隆阿夾擊於掛車河，盡破棠梨山、尊上庵、香鋪街、望鶴墩賊壘，斬馘無算，追奔二十餘里，玉成走廬江。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng came with a hundred thousand to relieve the city; Xuyi and Duo Long'a struck from both sides at Guache River, completely broke the rebel ramparts at Tanglishan, Zunshang'an, Xiangpujie, and Wanghedun, killed and captured beyond counting, pursued in flight more than twenty li, and Yucheng fled to Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng came to relieve the city with a hundred thousand men; Xuyi and Duo Long'a caught him at Guache River, stormed the forts at Tanglishan, Zunshang'an, Xiangpujie, and Wanghedun, killed countless enemy, pursued them twenty li, and drove Yucheng back to Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，賜二品頂戴。

translations.literal: When victory was reported he was granted the second-rank official button.
translations.idiomatic: News of the victory brought him the second-rank official button.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢安徽巡撫，疏言：「陳玉成圖解安慶之圍，悉銳西竄，以攻我之所必救。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Anhui governor and memorialized: "Chen Yucheng plans to relieve the siege of Anqing, gathering all his elite to flee westward to attack where we must certainly go to save.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was made governor of Anhui and wrote, "Chen Yucheng means to break the siege of Anqing by marching west in full strength to strike where we must relieve.

sentences.zh: 湖北為眾軍根本，臣宜提師回援，不能遽任皖撫之事。」

translations.literal: Hubei is the root of all armies; your servant ought to lead troops back to the relief and cannot immediately undertake the duties of Anhui governor."
translations.idiomatic: Hubei is the base of all our armies; I must march back to relieve it and cannot yet take up the governorship of Anhui."

sentences.zh: 比抵武昌，賊已陷黃州、德安兩府五縣，乃會彭玉麟水師夾攻孝感，乘夜縱火，復其城，進攻德安，穴地道克之。

translations.literal: When he reached Wuchang the rebels had already seized five counties in Huangzhou and De'an prefectures; he then joined Peng Yulin's naval forces in a pincer attack on Xiaogan, set fire by night, recovered the city, advanced to attack De'an, and captured it by mining tunnels.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Wuchang the enemy had taken five counties in Huangzhou and De'an; he joined Peng Yulin's fleet in a night assault on Xiaogan, retook the city by fire, then mined and took De'an.

sentences.zh: 武昌、通城、咸寧、蒲圻諸縣相繼皆下，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Wuchang, Tongcheng, Xianning, Puchi, and other counties were taken in succession, and he was granted the yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang, Tongcheng, Xianning, Puchi, and other counties fell in turn, and he received the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼病歿，詔授續宜湖北巡撫，駐黃州督師。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi died of illness; an edict appointed Xuyi governor of Hubei, encamped at Huangzhou to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Linyi died, Xuyi was appointed governor of Hubei and stationed at Huangzhou to command the armies.

sentences.zh: 捻匪犯光化、穀城、均州及棗陽、襄陽，皆擊走之，調安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: Nian bandits invaded Guanghua, Gucheng, Junzhou, and Zaoyang and Xiangyang; all were beaten off; he was transferred to Anhui governor.
translations.idiomatic: He drove off Nian raids on Guanghua, Gucheng, Junzhou, Zaoyang, and Xiangyang, then was transferred to governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，命幫辦欽差大臣勝保軍務。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was ordered to assist Imperial Commissioner Sheng Bao in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he was ordered to assist Imperial Commissioner Sheng Bao.

sentences.zh: 時苗沛霖叛服無常，勝保袒之。

translations.literal: At this time Miao Peilin rebelled and submitted without constancy, and Sheng Bao shielded him.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Peilin was shifting between rebellion and submission, and Sheng Bao protected him.

sentences.zh: 詔密詢續宜剿撫機宜，覆疏略謂：「苗沛霖官至道員，公犯不韙，圍撫臣於壽州，陷其城，屠其眾。

translations.literal: An edict secretly inquired of Xuyi the opportune measures for suppression and pacification; his reply memorial said in summary: "Miao Peilin reached the rank of circuit intendant, openly committed grave offenses, besieged the governor at Shouzhou, seized its city, and slaughtered its people.
translations.idiomatic: The court secretly asked Xuyi how to handle Miao; he replied in part, "Miao Peilin rose to circuit intendant, then openly rebelled, besieged the governor at Shouzhou, took the city, and massacred its people.

sentences.zh: 乃復詭言求撫，此豈足信？

translations.literal: Yet he again spoke deceitfully requesting pacification—how can this be trusted?
translations.idiomatic: Now he pretends to seek peace again—who can believe that?

sentences.zh: 不過假稱反正，號召近縣，養成羽翼。

translations.literal: It is nothing but falsely claiming to return to loyalty, summoning nearby counties, and nurturing wings of support.
translations.idiomatic: He only feigns loyalty to rally the neighboring counties and build his strength.

sentences.zh: 若正彼叛逆之名，人人得而誅之。

translations.literal: If we set right the name of his rebellion, everyone may kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim him a rebel, and any man may strike him down.

sentences.zh: 寬其黨羽，使為我用，彼勢孤，終成擒耳。」

translations.literal: Be lenient to his followers and make them serve us; he will be isolated in power and in the end will be captured."
translations.idiomatic: Win over his followers and use them; isolated, he will be taken in the end."

sentences.zh: 上韙之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 續宜駐臨淮，令提督成大吉、總兵蕭慶衍，渡淮援潁州，破捻匪張洛行於大橋集，潁州圍解。

translations.literal: Xuyi encamped at Linhuai, ordered Brigadier Cheng Daji and Commander Xiao Qingyan to cross the Huai to relieve Yingzhou, defeated the Nian bandit Zhang Luoxing at Daqiaoji, and the siege of Yingzhou was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Xuyi stationed himself at Linhuai and sent Brigadier Cheng Daji and Commander Xiao Qingyan across the Huai to relieve Yingzhou; they defeated the Nian leader Zhang Luoxing at Daqiaoji and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 又令蔣凝學克霍丘，撫綏各圩，解散逆黨。

translations.literal: He also ordered Jiang Ningxue to capture Huoqiu, pacify the various stockaded hamlets, and disband the rebel faction.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jiang Ningxue to take Huoqiu, pacify the walled villages, and disband the rebel bands.

sentences.zh: 沛霖懾湘軍兵威，請討捻自贖，而勝保終欲養沛霖以自重，轉嫉湘軍，勢不相下。

translations.literal: Peilin feared the Hunan army's military prestige and requested to suppress the Nian to redeem himself, but Sheng Bao ultimately wished to nurture Peilin to increase his own weight, turned jealous of the Hunan army, and the two sides would not yield to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Peilin feared the Hunan army and offered to fight the Nian to redeem himself, but Sheng Bao wanted to keep him as a pawn and grew jealous of the Hunan forces; the two factions were at odds.

sentences.zh: 會袁甲三以病請去，命續宜代為欽差大臣，督辦安徽全省軍務。

translations.literal: It happened that Yuan Jiasan requested leave due to illness; Xuyi was ordered to replace him as Imperial Commissioner supervising military affairs for all Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Jiasan resigned on grounds of illness, Xuyi was made Imperial Commissioner in charge of all military affairs in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 續宜旋丁母憂，奪情留軍。

translations.literal: Xuyi soon entered mourning for his mother; his grief was set aside and he remained with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Xuyi was soon in mourning for his mother but was kept on duty by imperial dispensation.

sentences.zh: 三疏陳謝，舉唐訓方自代，允假百日。

translations.literal: Three times he memorialized declining, recommended Tang Xunfang to replace him, and was granted a hundred days' leave.
translations.idiomatic: He declined three times, recommended Tang Xunfang as his replacement, and was granted a hundred days' leave.

sentences.zh: 回籍病咯血，六次詔促起視師，不能赴，二年十一月，卒於家。

translations.literal: Returning to his native place he fell ill coughing blood; six edicts urged him to rise and oversee the army but he could not go; in the eleventh month of the second year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home with a consumptive cough; six edicts ordered him back to command, but he could not go; he died at home in the eleventh month of the second year.

sentences.zh: 詔加恩依總督軍營病故例賜卹，立功地方及原籍建專祠，諡勇毅。

translations.literal: An edict added favor according to the precedent for a governor-general dying of illness in camp, granted posthumous gifts, built a special shrine at the place of merit and in his native place, and gave the posthumous title Yongyi.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted posthumous honors on the precedent for a governor-general dying in camp, ordered temples at the scene of his service and in his home county, and gave him the posthumous name Yongyi (Brave and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 賜其父人蓡四兩，地方官以時存問。

translations.literal: His father was granted four taels of ginseng; local officials were to inquire after him at the proper seasons.
translations.idiomatic: His father received four taels of ginseng, with orders that local officials visit him regularly.

sentences.zh: 子光英，予官直隸州知州。

translations.literal: His son Guangying was granted the office of prefect of Zhili prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guangying was granted the post of prefect of Zhizhou in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 續宜治軍嚴整，與兄續賓同負重名。

translations.literal: Xuyi governed the army with strict order and together with his elder brother Xubin bore a heavy reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Xuyi ran a tight army and shared his brother's great fame.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓嘗論其昆弟為人，續賓好蓋覆人過，續宜則嫉惡稍嚴。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan once discussed the brothers' characters: Xubin liked to cover others' faults; Xuyi was somewhat stricter in hating evil.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan once compared the brothers: Xubin was inclined to cover others' faults, Xuyi somewhat sterner in condemning wrong.

sentences.zh: 續賓戰必身先，驍果縝密，續宜則規畫大計，不校一戰之利，及其成功一也。

translations.literal: Xubin in battle always took the lead personally, was fierce and resolute and meticulous; Xuyi planned the great strategy and did not contend over the profit of a single battle—yet in their success they were one.
translations.idiomatic: Xubin always led the charge, fierce and meticulous in detail; Xuyi planned the larger campaign and cared little for a single engagement—yet in the end they achieved the same renown.

sentences.zh: =王珍=王珍，字璞山，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: =Wang Zhen= Wang Zhen, styled Pushan, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen, styled Pushan, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 諸生，從羅澤南學，任俠好奇。

translations.literal: A licentiate, he studied under Luo Zeren and was chivalrous, taking delight in adventure.
translations.idiomatic: He held licentiate rank, studied with Luo Zeren, and was adventurous and fond of feats of daring.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，粵匪犯長沙，上書縣令硃孫詒，請練鄉兵從澤南教練，屯馬垞埔，以團防勞敘縣丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, Guangdong rebels attacked Changsha. He submitted a memorial to the county magistrate Zhu Sunyi requesting to train local militia under Zeren's instruction, encamped at Macuopu, and was rewarded for militia defense service with appointment as assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdong rebels besieged Changsha in the second year of Xianfeng, he petitioned County Magistrate Zhu Sunyi to raise local militia trained by Luo Zeren. Stationed at Macuopu, he earned appointment as assistant magistrate for his service in organizing local defense.

sentences.zh: 剿桂東土匪有功。

translations.literal: He had merit in suppressing bandits in Guidong.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself suppressing bandits in Guidong.

sentences.zh: 廣東邊境匪犯興寧，率死士百人馳擊，殪賊甚多，累擢同知直隸州。

translations.literal: When bandits on the Guangdong border attacked Xingning, he led a hundred dare-to-die troops in a rapid strike, killed many rebels, and was repeatedly promoted to sub-prefect of Zhili Department.
translations.idiomatic: When border bandits raided Xingning, he rushed forward with a hundred picked volunteers, killed many of the enemy, and rose through repeated promotions to sub-prefect of Zhili Department.

sentences.zh: 三年，羅澤南援江西，初戰多死傷。

translations.literal: In the third year, Luo Zeren went to aid Jiangxi; in the first battles there were many dead and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Luo Zeren marched to relieve Jiangxi, the opening engagements cost heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 珍請於曾國籓，增募三千人，將往援，會南昌圍解。

translations.literal: Zhen requested of Zeng Guofan to raise an additional three thousand men and was about to go to the relief when the siege of Nanchang was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen asked Zeng Guofan to recruit three thousand more troops and was preparing to march to the rescue when the siege of Nanchang was already broken.

sentences.zh: 國籓議裁汰其軍，巡撫駱秉章見所募勇可用，留二千四百人防湖南。

translations.literal: Guofan proposed to reduce his army, but Governor Luo Bingzhang, seeing that the recruits he had raised were usable, retained twenty-four hundred men to defend Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan planned to disband most of the force, but Governor Luo Bingzhang judged the new recruits effective and kept twenty-four hundred men to guard Hunan.

sentences.zh: 珍精於訓練，令士卒縛鐵瓦習超距。

translations.literal: Zhen was skilled at training and ordered his soldiers to bind iron tiles and practice leaping exercises.
translations.idiomatic: An expert drillmaster, he had his men train by strapping on iron weights and practicing leaps and vaults.

sentences.zh: 自以意為陣法，進退變動，異於諸軍。

translations.literal: He devised battle formations according to his own ideas; advances, retreats, and changes differed from those of other armies.
translations.idiomatic: He invented his own tactical formations, and the way his units advanced, withdrew, and shifted was unlike anything in the other Hunan forces.

sentences.zh: 四年，粵匪踞岳州，珍由湘陰進攻，敗賊於杉木橋，乘勝克岳州，曾國籓率水陸軍並至。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Guangdong rebels occupied Yuezhou. Zhen advanced from Xiangyin, defeated the rebels at Shanmu Bridge, and taking advantage of victory captured Yuezhou, as Zeng Guofan arrived with combined land and river forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Taiping forces held Yuezhou, Zhen advanced from Xiangyin, routed them at Shanmu Bridge, and pressed on to retake the city just as Zeng Guofan's combined army arrived by land and water.

sentences.zh: 珍出境進剿，遇賊羊樓峒，失利，賊躡其後，岳州复陷。

translations.literal: Zhen crossed the border in pursuit and met the rebels at Yanglou Cave; he was defeated, the rebels followed close behind, and Yuezhou again fell.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the pursuit beyond Hunan, he met the enemy at Yanglou Cave and was beaten; the rebels trailed him home, and Yuezhou fell once more.

sentences.zh: 珍所部死者千人，坐輕進奪職，留營效力。

translations.literal: A thousand of Zhen's men died; for rash advance he was stripped of office but retained in camp to serve.
translations.idiomatic: His command lost a thousand men. Punished for reckless pursuit, he was dismissed from rank but allowed to remain with the army and redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 既而羅澤南從國籓東征，珍收集散眾，留未遣，駱秉章令率五百人徇郴州。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Luo Zeren followed Guofan on the eastern campaign; Zhen gathered the scattered troops and was kept from being sent away; Luo Bingzhang ordered him to lead five hundred men to attack Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Zeren marched east with Zeng Guofan, Zhen was kept behind to rally stragglers. Luo Bingzhang then sent him with five hundred men against Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 時兩廣交界土匪蜂起，硃連英、胡有祿最強，各擁萬人，稱王號，時時擾湖南邊境，珍與參將周雲耀協防江華，數擊走之。

translations.literal: At the time bandits swarmed at the junction of Guangdong and Guangxi; Zhu Lianying and Hu Youlu were strongest, each commanding ten thousand men and assuming royal titles, constantly harassing the Hunan border. Zhen and Assistant General Zhou Yunyao jointly defended Jianghua and repeatedly drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were erupting all along the Guangdong-Guangxi frontier. Zhu Lianying and Hu Youlu were the most powerful, each commanding ten thousand men and proclaiming himself king. They repeatedly raided Hunan. Zhen and Assistant General Zhou Yunyao held Jianghua together and beat them back again and again.

sentences.zh: 援道州，解其圍。

translations.literal: He went to relieve Daozhou and lifted its siege.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to relieve Daozhou and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 策賊必乘虛襲江華，日馳百餘里，先至，待賊至迎擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Concluding that the rebels would seize the opportunity to strike Jianghua, he rode more than a hundred li in a day, arrived first, waited for the rebels to come, and met them with an attack that broke them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Anticipating a strike at undefended Jianghua, he forced a march of more than a hundred li in a day, arrived first, and when the enemy appeared met them head-on in a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 進搗桃州，出龍虎關，破恭城賊於栗木街，回軍解寧遠、藍山圍。

translations.literal: He advanced to strike Taozhou, issued through Longhu Pass, defeated Gongcheng rebels at Limu Street, and on returning his army lifted the sieges of Ningyuan and Lanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Pushing into Taozhou through Longhu Pass, he routed the Gongcheng rebels at Limu Street, then swung back to raise the sieges of Ningyuan and Lanshan.

sentences.zh: 別賊掠零陵，周雲耀困於隘。

translations.literal: Another band of rebels plundered Lingling, and Zhou Yunyao was trapped in a narrow pass.
translations.idiomatic: When a separate rebel force pillaged Lingling, Zhou Yunyao found himself pinned in a defile.

sentences.zh: 珍率數十人馳進，令曰：「寇眾，退且死！」

translations.literal: Zhen led several dozen men in a rapid advance and ordered: "The enemy are numerous—if we retreat we die!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen galloped forward with only a few dozen men and shouted: "The enemy outnumber us—retreat means death!

sentences.zh: 據險夾擊，逐北數十里，轉戰深入九嶷山，賊氛漸清，復原官，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Seizing advantageous ground he attacked from both flanks, pursued the routed enemy for several dozen li, fought deep into Jiuyi Mountain, the rebel threat gradually subsided, his original rank was restored, and he was awarded the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the high ground, struck from both flanks, and pursued the rout for miles into Jiuyi Mountain. As rebel activity waned, his rank was restored and he was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 五年，土匪何賤苟勾結硃連英陷富川、江華，進犯永明。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the bandit He Jiangou joined with Zhu Lianying to seize Fuchuan and Jianghua and advanced to attack Yongming.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, the bandit He Jiangou allied with Zhu Lianying, captured Fuchuan and Jianghua, and marched on Yongming.

sentences.zh: 珍偕周雲耀往剿，迭敗之。

translations.literal: Zhen together with Zhou Yunyao went to suppress them and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Zhou Yunyao pursued them and inflicted defeat after defeat.

sentences.zh: 連州匪自龍虎關來犯，勢甚張，疾趨迎擊，殪賊二千，擢知府。

translations.literal: Bandits from Lianzhou came to attack through Longhu Pass with very strong momentum; he hurried to meet them, killed two thousand rebels, and was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Lianzhou bandits poured through Longhu Pass in great force, he rushed to intercept them, killed two thousand, and was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 餘賊走陷灌陽，復由全州襲陷東安。
