translations.literal: The remaining rebels fled, seized Guanyang, and again from Quanzhou raided and seized Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors fled, overrunning Guanyang and then striking Dong'an from Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 珍會廣西軍克灌陽，馳至東安城下，環攻兩月，始克之。

translations.literal: Zhen joined Guangxi forces to capture Guanyang, rushed to beneath the walls of Dong'an, besieged it for two months, and finally took it.
translations.idiomatic: Linking up with Guangxi troops, he retook Guanyang, then raced to Dong'an and invested the city for two months before it fell.

sentences.zh: 賊竄出，合胡有祿，將入四明山。

translations.literal: The rebels fled out, joined Hu Youlu, and were about to enter Siming Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The defeated rebels slipped away, joined Hu Youlu, and made for the Siming Mountains.

sentences.zh: 分路抄襲，擒有祿，焚山中賊巢，餘黨悉盡。

translations.literal: He sent columns to outflank and strike, captured Youlu, burned the rebel nests in the mountains, and the remaining followers were completely wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Splitting his force to surround them, he captured Hu Youlu, burned the mountain hideouts, and exterminated the last of the band.

sentences.zh: 時別賊何祿踞郴州，陳義和踞桂陽，分擾永興、茶陵、耒陽，窺衡州。

translations.literal: At the time another rebel He Lu occupied Chenzhou, Chen Yihe occupied Guiyang, and they separately harassed Yongxing, Chaling, and Leiyang, eyeing Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the rebel He Lu held Chenzhou and Chen Yihe held Guiyang; their raids across Yongxing, Chaling, and Leiyang threatened Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 珍增募至千五百人，分兵守耒陽，自率千人攻桂陽，再戰克之。

translations.literal: Zhen increased recruitment to fifteen hundred men, divided troops to guard Leiyang, personally led a thousand men to attack Guiyang, and after two battles captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen expanded his force to fifteen hundred names, posted troops at Leiyang, and personally led a thousand men against Guiyang, which fell after two hard fights.

sentences.zh: 賊聚糧於瓦蜜坪，火其屯，出奇兵攻郴州，賊遁走尚萬餘，合鄉團邀擊於黃沙堡，追至兩廣墟，賊方食，縱擊殲之。

translations.literal: The rebels gathered grain at Wamiping; he burned their depot, sent a surprise force to attack Chenzhou, the rebels fled with more than ten thousand still remaining, he joined local militia to intercept at Huangshabao, pursued to Liangguangxu where the rebels were eating, and launched an attack that annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: He burned the rebel grain depot at Wamiping, then surprised Chenzhou with a flanking column. More than ten thousand rebels fled, but local militia blocked them at Huangshabao. Zhen pursued them to Liangguang Market, where he caught them at mealtime and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 乘勝破永明、江華踞賊，窮追至連州，硃連英僅以身跳免。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of victory he broke the rebels occupying Yongming and Jianghua, pursued relentlessly to Lianzhou, and Zhu Lianying escaped only with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory, he cleared Yongming and Jianghua and chased the enemy all the way to Lianzhou, where Zhu Lianying barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 六年春，又破賊於陽山，賊遁英德。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year he again defeated rebels at Yangshan; the rebels fled to Yingde.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year he routed another force at Yangshan and drove the survivors toward Yingde.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章上其功，迭詔嘉獎，予四品封典，以道員即選。

translations.literal: Luo Bingzhang reported his achievements; repeated edicts praised and rewarded him, granting a fourth-rank patent of nobility and immediate selection for a provincial commissioner post.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Bingzhang memorialized his record; the throne issued repeated commendations, a fourth-rank patent of nobility, and immediate appointment as a provincial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 珍專辦南防凡二年，湘、粵間諸匪誅殄幾盡，軍士死亡亦多。

translations.literal: Zhen devoted himself to southern defense for two years in all; bandits between Hunan and Guangdong were nearly all exterminated, but many soldiers also died.
translations.idiomatic: For two years Zhen held sole charge of Hunan's southern frontier. Rebels along the Hunan-Guangdong border were virtually wiped out, though at great cost in dead soldiers.

sentences.zh: 請假將還，會羅澤南卒於武昌，李續賓代將其軍，粵匪石達開自江西窺湖北，續賓招珍助剿。

translations.literal: He requested leave to return home; just then Luo Zeren died at Wuchang, Li Xubin replaced him in command of his army, the Guangdong rebel Shi Dakai from Jiangxi eyed Hubei, and Xubin recruited Zhen to assist in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When he applied for leave to go home, Luo Zeren died at Wuchang and Li Xubin took over his command. As Shi Dakai probed Hubei from Jiangxi, Xubin called Zhen back to help.

sentences.zh: 遂進屯岳州，轉戰崇陽、通城、通山、蒲圻，复四縣，殲賊首張康忠、陳華玉等，興國、大冶匪眾亦解散。

translations.literal: He then advanced and encamped at Yuezhou, fought at Chongyang, Tongcheng, Tongshan, and Puqi, recovered the four counties, exterminated rebel leaders Zhang Kangzhong, Chen Huayu, and others, and the bandit masses of Xingguo and Daye also dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed into Yuezhou and fought through Chongyang, Tongcheng, Tongshan, and Puqi, recovering all four counties. Rebel chiefs Zhang Kangzhong and Chen Huayu were killed, and bandit bands in Xingguo and Daye melted away.

sentences.zh: 武昌尋克復，加按察使銜，以湖北道員記名簡放，仍駐軍岳州。

translations.literal: Wuchang was soon recovered; he was given the rank of surveillance commissioner, named for selection and appointment as a Hubei circuit intendant, and still stationed his army at Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuchang was retaken, he received the rank of surveillance commissioner and nomination for a Hubei circuit post, while remaining encamped at Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，調援江西，五月，抵吉安。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to aid Jiangxi; in the fifth month he reached Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was ordered to Jiangxi and reached Ji'an in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 先是官軍水陸合圍吉安，其攻臨江者，亦掘長壕困賊。

translations.literal: Earlier the government armies had jointly besieged Ji'an by land and water; those attacking Linjiang had also dug long trenches to trap the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces had already invested Ji'an by land and water, while another column digging trenches around Linjiang was starving the defenders there.

sentences.zh: 賊渠胡壽階、何秉權率眾數万來援，據水東，與城賊夾江相望。

translations.literal: Rebel chiefs Hu Shoujie and He Bingquan led several tens of thousands to the relief, occupied Shuidong, and faced the rebels in the city across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel commanders Hu Shoujie and He Bingquan marched tens of thousands to the relief, seized Shuidong on the east bank, and faced the Ji'an garrison across the river.

sentences.zh: 珍沿贛江而南，自三曲灘濟，結營水東東南山上。

translations.literal: Zhen went south along the Gan River, crossed from Sanqu Beach, and established camp on the southeastern mountain of Shuidong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen marched south along the Gan, crossed at Sanqu Beach, and fortified a camp on the southeastern hills overlooking Shuidong.

sentences.zh: 賊鼓譟乘之，珍登望樓，令士卒築壘不輟，毋許仰視，賊疑不進。

translations.literal: The rebels beat drums and clamored to take advantage; Zhen mounted the watchtower, ordered the soldiers to build fortifications without cease and not to look up; the rebels suspected a trap and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels surged forward with drums and shouts. From the watchtower Zhen ordered his men to keep building ramparts and forbid them to look up. The enemy suspected an ambush and held back.

sentences.zh: 俄山後一軍出賊背，鼓聲起，築壘者投畚大呼馳擊，左右伏起，陣斬秉權，蹙賊眾於水，餘走水東。

translations.literal: Suddenly an army emerged from behind the mountain at the rebels' rear, drums sounded, those building fortifications threw down their baskets, shouted loudly, and charged; ambushes rose left and right, He Bingquan was slain in battle, the rebel masses were pressed into the water, and the remainder fled to Shuidong.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a hidden column burst from the hills behind the enemy. At the drumbeat the men building ramparts dropped their tools, shouted, and charged. Ambushers rose on both flanks. He Bingquan was killed in the melee, masses of rebels were driven into the river, and the rest fled toward Shuidong.

sentences.zh: 軍中方具餐，珍曰：「不克水東不遑食！」

translations.literal: The army was just preparing meals when Zhen said: "Until Shuidong is taken there is no time to eat!"
translations.idiomatic: As his troops were sitting down to eat, Zhen declared: "No meal until Shuidong falls!

sentences.zh: 揮軍搗賊壘。

translations.literal: He waved his army to storm the rebel fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered an assault on the rebel works.

sentences.zh: 都司易普照，勇士也，先登中砲殞，眾憤，爭入壘，殺賊數千，壽階遁。

translations.literal: Division Commander Yi Puzhao, a brave warrior, was first to ascend but was killed by cannon; the men were enraged, vied to enter the fortifications, killed several thousand rebels, and Shoujie fled.
translations.idiomatic: Division Commander Yi Puzhao, a fearless fighter, was first over the wall but fell to cannon fire. Enraged, the troops surged into the fort, killed thousands, and Hu Shoujie escaped.

sentences.zh: 珍渡江壁藤田，壽階自寧都、沙溪挾援眾來犯，珍分兵擊其左，自率百人搗其右，賊崩潰，蹙之瑤嶺，擒壽階，斬馘數千。

translations.literal: Zhen crossed the river and fortified at Tengtian; Shoujie from Ningdu and Shaxi brought relief forces to attack; Zhen divided troops to strike their left, personally led a hundred men to hit their right, the rebels collapsed, he pressed them to Yaoling, captured Shoujie, and killed several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen crossed the river and fortified Tengtian. When Hu Shoujie brought reinforcements from Ningdu and Shaxi, Zhen struck their left with a detachment and personally led a hundred men against their right. The rebel line collapsed; pressed to Yaoling, Hu Shoujie was captured and thousands were slain.

sentences.zh: 是役悍賊俘斬殆盡。

translations.literal: In this campaign the fierce rebels were captured and killed nearly to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: In that campaign the hardest rebel fighters were killed or captured almost to a man.

sentences.zh: 閏月，援賊復自寧都出永豐。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month relief rebels again came out from Ningdu toward Yongfeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month fresh rebel reinforcements marched from Ningdu toward Yongfeng.

sentences.zh: 珍以千二百人迎擊之，追至寧都之釣峰。

translations.literal: Zhen with twelve hundred men went to meet them in battle and pursued to Diaofeng in Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen met them with twelve hundred men and chased them to Diaofeng in Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 賊背水以拒，既敗，盡沒於水。

translations.literal: The rebels had their backs to the water to resist; once defeated, all were drowned in the water.
translations.idiomatic: With their backs to the river, the rebels made a stand but were driven into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 斬賊首蕭复勝等，拔難民萬餘；

translations.literal: He beheaded rebel chiefs Xiao Fusheng and others and rescued more than ten thousand civilian captives;
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leaders including Xiao Fusheng were killed, and more than ten thousand captives were freed;

sentences.zh: 六月，再破新城賊於東山壩，斬賊首張宗相等。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he again defeated Xinjiang rebels at Dongshanba and beheaded rebel chief Zhang Zongxiang and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he routed the Xinjiang rebels at Dongshan Dam and killed Zhang Zongxiang and other rebel leaders.

sentences.zh: 時悍賊楊輔清憤屢敗，糾眾十萬踞廣昌頭陂，誓決死戰。

translations.literal: At the time the fierce rebel Yang Fuqing, angry at repeated defeats, gathered a hundred thousand men and occupied Guangchang Toupi, vowing to fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: The hardened rebel Yang Fuqing, stung by one defeat after another, mustered a hundred thousand men at Guangchang Toupi and swore to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 珍笑曰：「賊聚此，可一鼓殲也！」

translations.literal: Zhen laughed and said: "The rebels have massed here—they can be wiped out in one stroke!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen laughed and said: "Gathered like this, they can be crushed in a single rush!

sentences.zh: 勒兵大戰，先馳馬陷陣，眾從之，賊大潰，逐北六十里，斬馘無算。

translations.literal: He marshaled his troops for a great battle, first galloped his horse into the enemy lines, the masses followed, the rebels were utterly routed, he pursued the fleeing enemy for sixty li, and the killed and captured were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He massed his troops for a pitched battle, spurred his horse into the enemy ranks first, and his men followed. The rebels broke completely; he chased them sixty li and the dead and captured were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，詔嘉獎，稱其以寡敵眾，殲除鉅憝，賜號給什蘭巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, an edict praised and rewarded him, stating that with few he had matched many and exterminated a great villain, and granted him the title Shilan Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: News of the victory brought an imperial commendation praising how he had defeated a vast enemy with a small force and destroyed a major rebel leader. He was granted the title Shilan Batulu.

sentences.zh: 方拔樂安，進規撫、建兩郡，會周鳳山兵潰吉安，乞援。

translations.literal: Just as he had taken Le'an and was advancing to target the two prefectures of Fuzhou and Jianzhou, Zhou Fengshan's army was routed at Ji'an and begged for relief.
translations.idiomatic: He had just taken Le'an and was planning moves against Fuzhou and Jianzhou when Zhou Fengshan's force collapsed at Ji'an and called for help.

sentences.zh: 珍令鄉團張己幟趨建昌，而潛返藤田規吉水。

translations.literal: Zhen ordered the local militia to raise his banners and hurry toward Jianchang, while secretly returning to Tengtian to target Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: He sent local militia toward Jianchang under his banners as a feint while slipping back to Tengtian to threaten Jishui.

sentences.zh: 楊輔清聞珍去，以七萬眾圍樂安。

translations.literal: Yang Fuqing heard that Zhen had departed and with seventy thousand men besieged Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Fuqing learned Zhen had left, he invested Le'an with seventy thousand men.

sentences.zh: 珍夜入城，誘賊至城下痛殲之。

translations.literal: Zhen entered the city by night, lured the rebels to the foot of the walls, and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen slipped into the city at night, drew the rebels under the walls, and slaughtered them.

sentences.zh: 輔清屯林頭，珍進擊，賊以馬隊數千突陣，令火箭射之，藤牌兵俯首砍馬足。

translations.literal: Fuqing encamped at Lintou; Zhen advanced to attack; the rebels sent several thousand cavalry to charge the formation; he ordered fire arrows shot at them; rattan-shield soldiers bowed their heads and cut at horses' legs.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuqing held Lintou, Zhen attacked. Thousands of rebel cavalry charged the line; he ordered fire arrows loosed, and rattan-shield men ducked low to hack at the horses' legs.

sentences.zh: 劉松山、易開俊左右合擊，自率精銳貫賊陣，斬級數千，獲馬三百匹，俘八百人，輔清遁走。

translations.literal: Liu Songshan and Yi Kaijun attacked jointly from left and right; he personally led picked troops through the rebel formation, severed several thousand heads, captured three hundred horses and eight hundred prisoners, and Fuqing fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Songshan and Yi Kaijun struck from both flanks while Zhen personally led an elite column through the rebel center. Thousands were killed, three hundred horses and eight hundred prisoners were taken, and Yang Fuqing fled.

sentences.zh: 珍感疾返樂安，九月，卒於軍，年僅三十有三。

translations.literal: Zhen, stricken with illness, returned to Le'an; in the ninth month he died in the army, aged only thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Stricken by illness, Zhen returned to Le'an and died in camp in the ninth month. He was only thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉獎紀律嚴明，身經數百戰，前後殺賊十餘萬，克復城池二十餘處，厥功甚偉，贈布政使銜，依二品從優議卹，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: An edict praised and rewarded his strict discipline, service through several hundred battles, killing more than a hundred thousand rebels before and after, recovering more than twenty cities and towns—his achievements were very great—posthumously granting the rank of administration commissioner, treating funeral honors at second rank with preferential consideration, and awarding a hereditary captaincy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended his iron discipline and record of hundreds of battles in which he had killed more than a hundred thousand rebels and recovered over twenty cities. For these signal achievements he was posthumously given the rank of administration commissioner, accorded second-rank funeral honors, and granted a hereditary captaincy.

sentences.zh: 江西、湖南建專祠，諡壯武。

translations.literal: Dedicated shrines were built in Jiangxi and Hunan; his posthumous title was Zhuangwu ("Valiant in War").
translations.idiomatic: Dedicated shrines were erected in Jiangxi and Hunan, and he was posthumously titled Zhuangwu, "Valiant in War."

sentences.zh: 珍貌不逾中人，膽力沉鷙，用兵好出奇制勝，馭眾嚴而有恩。

translations.literal: Zhen's appearance did not exceed that of an ordinary man; his courage and strength were deep and fierce; in using troops he favored surprise to achieve victory; in commanding the masses he was strict yet benevolent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was unremarkable in appearance, but his courage ran deep and cold. He won battles through surprise, and though strict with his men he treated them with genuine kindness.

sentences.zh: 所著有練勇芻言、陣法新編，皆出心得。

translations.literal: His writings included Draft Remarks on Training Braves and New Compilation of Battle Formations, all born of personal experience.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Draft Remarks on Training Braves and New Compilation of Battle Formations, both drawn from hard-won experience.

sentences.zh: 劉松山為湘軍後起名將，舊隸部下，後其軍皆用珍法。

translations.literal: Liu Songshan became a famous general of the Hunan Army in later years; he had formerly served under Zhen's command, and afterward his army all used Zhen's methods.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Songshan later became one of the Hunan Army's most celebrated generals. He had once served under Zhen, and afterward his entire command followed Zhen's drill and tactics.

sentences.zh: 珍既歿，所部歸其弟開化及張運蘭分統之。

translations.literal: After Zhen died, his command passed to his younger brother Kai Hua and Zhang Yunlan to command jointly in division.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhen's death his troops were divided between his younger brother Kai Hua and Zhang Yunlan.

sentences.zh: 弟開化，年十七從珍軍中，南防剿匪功最多，累擢知縣。

translations.literal: Younger brother Kai Hua, at age seventeen followed Zhen in the army; in southern defense and bandit suppression his achievements were greatest; he was repeatedly promoted to county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Kai Hua joined the army at seventeen. In the southern bandit campaigns he won more distinction than anyone and rose repeatedly to county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 及援江西，寧都釣峰之戰，率伏兵潛襲賊營，遂大捷，無戰不與。

translations.literal: When aiding Jiangxi, at the battle of Diaofeng in Ningdu he led hidden troops in a secret attack on the rebel camp and thereby achieved a great victory; there was no battle in which he did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi, at the battle of Diaofeng in Ningdu, he led an ambush that stormed the rebel camp and turned the day into a rout. He fought in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章疏陳其功，擢知府。

translations.literal: Luo Bingzhang memorialized stating his achievements and he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Bingzhang cited his record in a memorial, and he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 遂令分統珍軍，偕張運蘭攻吉安，連戰皆捷。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to share command of Zhen's army, and together with Zhang Yunlan attacked Ji'an; in successive battles all were victorious.
translations.idiomatic: He was then placed in joint command of Zhen's old army and, with Zhang Yunlan, attacked Ji'an in a string of victories.

sentences.zh: 八年，克樂安、宜黃、崇仁、南豐、建昌，擢道員，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he captured Le'an, Yihuang, Chongren, Nanfeng, and Jianchang, was promoted to circuit intendant, and given the rank of surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he took Le'an, Yihuang, Chongren, Nanfeng, and Jianchang, rose to circuit intendant, and received the rank of surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 病歸里。

translations.literal: Ill, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He went home on sick leave.

sentences.zh: 十年，左宗棠初出治軍，開化從之，戰鄱陽、樂平，皆有功。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when Zuo Zongtang first went out to command troops, Kai Hua followed him; at battles in Poyang and Leping he had achievements in both.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when Zuo Zongtang first took the field, Kai Hua served under him and distinguished himself at Poyang and Leping.

sentences.zh: 及宗棠大破李世賢於樂平，開化與劉典各當一路。

translations.literal: When Zongtang greatly defeated Li Shixian at Leping, Kai Hua and Liu Dian each held one route.
translations.idiomatic: At Zuo Zongtang's great victory over Li Shixian at Leping, Kai Hua and Liu Dian each commanded a separate column.

sentences.zh: 是役官軍不及萬，破賊十萬，稱奇捷，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: In that campaign the government army was less than ten thousand, broke a hundred thousand rebels, was called a miraculous victory, and he was given the rank of administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In that fight fewer than ten thousand government troops routed a hundred thousand rebels—a victory hailed as miraculous—and he received the rank of administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 江西既平，從宗棠援皖南。

translations.literal: After Jiangxi was pacified, he followed Zongtang to aid southern Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jiangxi was pacified, he marched with Zuo Zongtang to relieve southern Anhui.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He died in service in the eleventh year.

sentences.zh: 開化在軍先後八年，勇毅亞於其兄。

translations.literal: Kai Hua was in the army for eight years in all; in courage and resolution he was second to his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Kai Hua served eight years in all. In courage and resolve he ranked just below his brother.

sentences.zh: 詔優恤，予騎都尉世職，諡貞介。

translations.literal: An edict granted preferential funeral honors, awarded a hereditary captaincy, and gave the posthumous title Zhenjie ("Upright and Incorruptible").
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted him preferential funeral honors, a hereditary captaincy, and the posthumous title Zhenjie, "Upright and Incorruptible."

sentences.zh: =劉騰鴻=劉騰鴻，字峙衡，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: =Liu Tenghong= Liu Tenghong, styled Zhiheng, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tenghong, styled Zhiheng, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 少讀書，未遇，服賈江湖間。

translations.literal: In youth he studied books but did not meet with success; he traveled the rivers and lakes as a merchant.
translations.idiomatic: He studied as a youth but never passed the examinations and took to trade along the rivers.

sentences.zh: ，夜泊湘江，遇潰卒數十輩行掠，誘至湘潭，白縣令捕之，由是知名。

translations.literal: , mooring on the Xiang River at night, he encountered several dozen bands of routed soldiers roving and plundering, lured them to Xiangtan, reported to the magistrate to capture them, and thereby became known.
translations.idiomatic: One night, moored on the Xiang River, he encountered several dozen demoralized soldiers looting the countryside. He lured them to Xiangtan and had the magistrate arrest them, and thus made his name.

sentences.zh: 五年，巴陵土匪起，巡撫駱秉章令率五百人往戰於毛田，擒賊渠，又敗之於三林坳，散其黨，遂駐岳州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year bandits rose in Baling; Governor Luo Bingzhang ordered him to lead five hundred men to fight at Maotian, captured a rebel chief, again defeated them at Sanlin'ao, scattered their band, and then stationed at Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Baling in the fifth year, Governor Luo Bingzhang sent him with five hundred men to Maotian, where he captured a rebel chief, routed the band again at Sanlin'ao, broke up their following, and then stationed at Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 從羅澤南攻通城，攀堞登城，克之。

translations.literal: Following Luo Zeren to attack Tongcheng, he climbed the parapet and scaled the wall, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Marching with Luo Zeren against Tongcheng, he scaled the walls and helped take the city.

sentences.zh: 參將彭三元等戰歿崇陽，澤南調騰鴻往，而石達開驅悍賊二萬來撲，騰鴻與游擊普承堯夾擊破之。

translations.literal: Assistant General Peng Sanyuan and others died in battle at Chongyang; Zeren transferred Tenghong there, and Shi Dakai drove twenty thousand fierce rebels to attack; Tenghong together with Brigadier Pu Chengyao attacked from both sides and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: After Assistant General Peng Sanyuan was killed at Chongyang, Luo Zeren sent Tenghong to the front. Shi Dakai then threw twenty thousand hardened rebels into the attack, but Tenghong and Brigadier Pu Chengyao caught them in a pincer and broke them.

sentences.zh: 蒲圻賊壘臨河，騰鴻由寶塔山截渡河賊，直抵城下，與普承堯循環攻擊，克蒲圻。

translations.literal: The rebel fort at Puqi faced the river; Tenghong from Baota Mountain intercepted the river-crossing rebels, went straight to beneath the city walls, and with Pu Chengyao attacked in rotation until Puqi was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel works at Puqi lined the river. Tenghong cut off ferry traffic from Baota Mountain, pushed to the city walls, and with Pu Chengyao hammered the position from every side until Puqi fell.

sentences.zh: 連下咸寧，抵武昌。

translations.literal: In succession he took Xianning and reached Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on through Xianning to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 騰鴻偕蔣益澧為後隊，搜伏賊，殲斃甚眾。

translations.literal: Tenghong together with Jiang Yili served as the rear guard, searched out hidden rebels, and killed very many.
translations.idiomatic: Tenghong and Jiang Yili brought up the rear, flushed out ambushes, and killed a great many rebels.

sentences.zh: 論功，以從九品選用。

translations.literal: Assessing merit, he was selected for appointment at the rank of subordinate clerk of the ninth grade.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was appointed at the rank of subordinate clerk of the ninth grade.

sentences.zh: 羅澤南愛其才，令增募五百人當前敵。

translations.literal: Luo Zeren admired his talent and ordered him to raise an additional five hundred men to serve as the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by his ability, Luo Zeren had him recruit five hundred more men for the front line.

sentences.zh: 騰鴻遂師事澤南，列弟子籍。

translations.literal: Tenghong then took Zeren as his teacher in the master-disciple relationship and was enrolled among the disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Tenghong formally became Luo Zeren's disciple and was entered on the roster of his students.

sentences.zh: 攻克十字街、塘角賊壘，毀其船廠，進據小龜山。

translations.literal: He captured the rebel forts at Shizijie and Tangjiao, destroyed their shipyard, and advanced to occupy Xiaoguishan.
translations.idiomatic: He took the rebel forts at Shizijie and Tangjiao, destroyed their shipyard, and seized Xiaoguishan.

sentences.zh: 賊七八千由塘角沿湖而下，澤南自率中營出洪山西，令騰鴻出洪山東，夾擊，斃賊無算，蕩平賊壘。

translations.literal: Seven or eight thousand rebels came down along the lake from Tangjiao; Zeren personally led the central battalion out from the west of Hongshan, ordered Tenghong out from the east of Hongshan, attacked from both sides, killed rebels beyond counting, and swept the rebel forts flat.
translations.idiomatic: When seven or eight thousand rebels marched down the lakeshore from Tangjiao, Luo Zeren led the center out west of Hongshan while Tenghong struck from the east. Caught between them, the rebels were slaughtered and their forts were leveled.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼奏騰鴻身先陷陣，七戰皆在諸軍前，超擢知縣。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi memorialized that Tenghong personally led the charge into enemy lines, in seven battles was always ahead of the other armies, and he was exceptionally promoted to county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi reported that Tenghong had personally led the charge in seven consecutive battles, always out in front of the other columns, and he was promoted directly to county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 六年春，賊踞賽湖以阻官軍，騰鴻與戰於堤上，追及長虹橋，遇伏，賊七倍我，奮擊，殺賊五六百。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year rebels occupied Saihu to block the government army; Tenghong fought them on the embankment, pursued to Changhong Bridge, encountered an ambush—the rebels were seven times their number—he fought fiercely and killed five or six hundred rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year rebels held Saihu to block the army's advance. Tenghong fought them on the dike and pursued to Changhong Bridge, where ambushers outnumbered his men seven to one. He fought on regardless and killed five or six hundred.

sentences.zh: 羅澤南欲扼窯灣，賊出爭，大戰於小龜山，斬級六百，遂偕李續賓同駐其地。

translations.literal: Luo Zeren wished to hold Yaowan in check; the rebels came out to contest it, and a great battle was fought at Xiaoguishan; six hundred heads were cut, and he then together with Li Xubin jointly encamped at that place.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zeren sought to seize Yaowan, but the rebels sallied out to oppose him. At Xiaoguishan a major battle ensued in which six hundred of the enemy were slain, after which he and Li Xubin established camp there together.

sentences.zh: 騰鴻所將號湘後營，樹黑幟，賊望見輒走。

translations.literal: What Tenghong commanded was called the Hunan Rear Battalion; it raised black banners, and whenever rebels saw them they at once fled.
translations.idiomatic: Tenghong's command, known as the Hunan Rear Battalion, flew black standards; rebels fled at the mere sight of them.

sentences.zh: 會江西軍事棘，胡林翼令騰鴻率所部千人從曾國華赴援瑞州，道為賊梗，轉戰而前，連捷於羊樓峒、分水坳，擒斬偽總制三十餘人，克上高、新昌。

translations.literal: Just then Jiangxi military affairs were thorny; Hu Linyi ordered Tenghong to lead his thousand men to follow Zeng Guohua to aid Ruizhou; the route was blocked by rebels, so they fought their way forward, winning successive victories at Yanglou'dong and Fenshui'ao, capturing and killing more than thirty false brigade-generals, and capturing Shanggao and Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs in Jiangxi had become critical. Hu Linyi ordered Tenghong to lead his thousand-man force with Zeng Guohua to relieve Ruizhou. Rebels blocked the route, but they fought through, winning successive victories at Yanglou'dong and Fenshui'ao, capturing and executing more than thirty rebel brigade-generals, and taking Shanggao and Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 七月，進攻瑞州，郡治有南北二城，中貫一河，聯以長橋。

translations.literal: In the seventh month they advanced to attack Ruizhou; the prefectural seat had north and south twin cities, with a river running through the middle, linked by a long bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they advanced on Ruizhou. The prefectural seat comprised twin walled cities north and south of a river, joined by a long bridge.

sentences.zh: 先拔南城，賊酋韋昌輝自臨江來援，軍容甚盛。

translations.literal: They first captured the southern city; the rebel chieftain Wei Changhui came from Linjiang to aid, and his army's appearance was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: They first took the southern city. Wei Changhui, a rebel chief, marched from Linjiang to relieve it with an imposing force.

sentences.zh: 騰鴻曰：「是羊質虎皮，不久見鞹。

translations.literal: Tenghong said: "This is sheep's substance with tiger's skin; before long the hide will show.
translations.idiomatic: Tenghong said, "They are sheep in tigers' clothing—the pelt will soon be stripped away.

sentences.zh: 宜乘其敝攻之。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to take advantage of their exhaustion and attack them."
translations.idiomatic: We should strike while they are spent."

sentences.zh: 相持旬日，賊氣衰。

translations.literal: After ten days of stalemate, rebel morale waned.
translations.idiomatic: After a standoff of ten days, rebel spirits flagged.

sentences.zh: 乃從北岸渡兵抄其後，與南城兵夾擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Then from the north bank troops were ferried across to outflank their rear, and together with the southern-city troops attacked from both sides, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were then ferried from the north bank to strike the enemy's rear, and in concert with the forces at the southern city attacked from both sides, routing them completely.

sentences.zh: 偽指揮黃姓來援，列陣出岡，兩軍對峙。

translations.literal: A false brigade-commander surnamed Huang came to aid, drew up battle lines and came out onto the ridge; the two armies faced each other in confrontation.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel brigade-commander surnamed Huang arrived to reinforce them and deployed his men on a ridge; the two armies stood facing each other.

sentences.zh: 別賊馳截我後路，圖夾攻，俟其近，發劈山砲擊之，再至，皆擊退，追奔三十里。

translations.literal: Separate rebels galloped to cut off our rear route, intending a pincer attack; waiting until they were near, mountain-splitting cannon were fired at them; when they came again, all were beaten back, and the pursuit ran thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Another rebel force rode to cut off their line of retreat and attempt a pincer. As the enemy drew near, mountain guns opened fire. When they returned, they were driven off again, and the pursuit continued thirty li.

sentences.zh: 石達開適自九江來，勒賊復還，築五壘於東北。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai happened to come from Jiujiang, compelled the rebels to return again, and built five forts in the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai arrived from Jiujiang, rallied the rebels, and erected five fortifications in the northeast.

sentences.zh: 騰鴻曰：「不急破之，壘成則難制矣。」

translations.literal: Tenghong said: "If they are not quickly broken, once the forts are complete they will be hard to control."
translations.idiomatic: Tenghong said, "If we do not smash them quickly, once those fortifications are finished they will be hard to subdue."

sentences.zh: 令楚軍防城賊，江軍進剿，自率死士三百督戰。

translations.literal: He ordered the Chu army to guard against the city rebels, the Jiang army to advance in suppression, and personally led three hundred dare-to-die soldiers to supervise the battle.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Hunan troops to hold the rebels in the city at bay while the Jiangxi army pressed the attack, personally leading three hundred shock troops into battle.

sentences.zh: 賊見兵少，先犯之，三百人植立無聲，伺近乃發砲，凡衝突六次不為動，賊氣沮，諸營效力猛攻，賊大敗，盡平其壘。

translations.literal: The rebels saw the troops were few and first attacked them; the three hundred men stood planted in silence; waiting until the enemy was near they fired cannon; in all they charged six times without moving; rebel morale was crushed; the various camps exerted themselves in fierce attack; the rebels were greatly defeated and all their forts were leveled.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how few they were, the rebels attacked first. The three hundred men stood silently in place until the enemy drew near, then opened fire with artillery. They held firm through six charges without budging. With rebel spirits broken, the other camps joined the assault. The rebels were routed and all five fortifications were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，擢直隸州知州，歸江西補用，賜號衝勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was promoted to prefect of Zhili Prefecture, assigned for service in Jiangxi upon return, and granted the title Chongyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: News of the victory reached the throne. He was promoted to prefect of Zhili Prefecture, assigned to Jiangxi service, and granted the title Chongyong Batulu ("Fearless Brave").

sentences.zh: 自克南城後，賊萃於北城。

translations.literal: After capturing the southern city, the rebels gathered at the northern city.
translations.idiomatic: After the southern city fell, the rebels concentrated in the northern city.

sentences.zh: 騰鴻欲斷其接濟，取南城磚石築壘造橋，賊來爭，且戰且築，又於北岸石封嶺築新城以逼之。

translations.literal: Tenghong wished to cut off their supply lines; he took brick and stone from the southern city to build forts and construct a bridge; rebels came to contest; fighting while building; also on the north bank at Shifengling he built a new city to press them.
translations.idiomatic: Tenghong sought to sever their supply lines. Using bricks and stone from the southern city, he built fortifications and a bridge under fire, fighting as he built. He also erected a new fortified position at Shifengling on the north bank to tighten the pressure.

sentences.zh: 七年春，曾國籓巡視瑞州，用騰鴻議，為長壕三十里，絕賊餉道。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year Zeng Guofan inspected Ruizhou, adopted Tenghong's proposal, and dug a long trench thirty li to cut off rebel supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year, Zeng Guofan inspected Ruizhou and, following Tenghong's plan, had a thirty-li trench dug to sever the rebels' supply lines.

sentences.zh: 國籓尋以喪返湖南，囑騰鴻主南路軍事。

translations.literal: Guofan soon returned to Hunan for mourning and charged Tenghong to take charge of southern-route military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan soon returned to Hunan to observe mourning and entrusted Tenghong with command of operations on the southern front.

sentences.zh: 先後遏賊於馬鞍嶺、陰岡嶺，戰皆捷，於是會諸軍克袁州、分宜、上高、新喻。

translations.literal: In succession he checked the rebels at Ma'anling and Yingangling, every battle victorious; thus rallying the armies he captured Yuanzhou, Fenyi, Shanggao, and Xinyu.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly checked the rebels at Ma'anling and Yingangling, winning every engagement, and then joined the allied armies in capturing Yuanzhou, Fenyi, Shanggao, and Xinyu.

sentences.zh: 劉長佑與賊戰於羅防，不利，騰鴻往援，擊敗之。

translations.literal: Liu Changyou fought rebels at Luofang with an unfavorable outcome; Tenghong went to aid and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changyou met defeat fighting rebels at Luofang; Tenghong marched to his relief and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 七月，回攻瑞州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he returned to attack Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he resumed the assault on Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 時李續賓進兵九江，胡林翼疏調騰鴻回湖北。

translations.literal: At that time Li Xubin was advancing on Jiujiang; Hu Linyi memorialized to transfer Tenghong back to Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xubin was then advancing on Jiujiang, and Hu Linyi submitted a memorial requesting Tenghong's recall to Hubei.

sentences.zh: 騰鴻以功在垂成，先分兵應之，而攻城益力，奪南門砲臺，复撲東門，毀其城樓，身自督戰，中槍子五，臥不能起。

translations.literal: Tenghong, because success was near at hand, first sent part of his force to respond, but pressed the siege with greater force, seized the southern gate gun platform, again stormed the eastern gate, destroyed its tower, personally supervised the battle, was struck by five bullets, and lay unable to rise.
translations.idiomatic: With victory within reach, Tenghong detached part of his force to answer the recall but pressed the assault harder. He seized the gun emplacement at the southern gate and again stormed the eastern gate, destroying its tower. Leading from the front, he was hit by five bullets and collapsed.

sentences.zh: 次日，裹創舁往，城垂克，忽中砲，洞穿左脅，移時殞。

translations.literal: The next day, wounds bound, he was carried forward; the city was on the verge of capture when suddenly he was struck by cannon, pierced through the left flank, and after a time died.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, his wounds bandaged, he was carried forward to the front again. The city was nearly taken when a cannonball pierced his left side; he died shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 語弟騰鶴曰：「城不下，無斂我！」

translations.literal: He told his younger brother Tenghe: "If the city is not taken, do not bury me!"
translations.idiomatic: He told his brother Tenghe, "Do not bury me until the city has fallen!"

sentences.zh: 一軍皆泣，冒砲火登城，斬殺悍賊過半，即夕克瑞州，迎騰鴻屍入城治喪。

translations.literal: The whole army wept; braving cannon fire they scaled the walls, killed more than half the fierce rebels, and that very evening captured Ruizhou, brought Tenghong's corpse into the city, and arranged the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The entire army wept. Braving cannon fire, they scaled the walls and cut down more than half the rebel garrison. That very night they took Ruizhou, brought Tenghong's body into the city, and laid him to rest.

sentences.zh: 事聞，卹典加等，依道員例，予騎都尉世職，於瑞州建專祠，予其父母正四品封典。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, funeral honors were raised a grade; following the pattern for circuit intendant, a hereditary captaincy was granted; a dedicated shrine was built at Ruizhou; his parents were granted fourth-rank posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, his funeral honors were raised. He was granted a hereditary captaincy at the rank of a circuit intendant, a memorial shrine was erected at Ruizhou, and his parents received fourth-rank honorary titles.

sentences.zh: 洎江南平，曾國籓追論前功，詔嘉其忠勇邁倫，加恩予諡武烈。

translations.literal: When the Jiangnan region was pacified, Zeng Guofan reviewed his earlier merits; an edict praised his loyalty and courage as surpassing others, and added grace by granting the posthumous title Wulie.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiangnan region was pacified, Zeng Guofan commended his earlier service. An edict praised his loyalty and valor as surpassing the ordinary and granted him the posthumous title Wulie ("Martial and Stern").

sentences.zh: 弟騰鶴，隨軍將中營。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tenghe followed the army and commanded the central battalion.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tenghe served in the army as commander of the central battalion.

sentences.zh: 先數月，因攻城傷左臂，創甚。

translations.literal: Several months earlier, in assaulting the city he was wounded in the left arm; the wound was severe.
translations.idiomatic: Several months earlier he had been seriously wounded in the left arm while assaulting the city.

sentences.zh: 騰鴻命歸，不可。

translations.literal: Tenghong ordered him to return home; he would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Tenghong ordered him to withdraw, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 及騰鴻殞於陣，騰鶴號泣督戰，克竟厥功，遂代將其軍。

translations.literal: When Tenghong died in battle, Tenghe wept aloud while directing the fight, completed that achievement, and then took command of his army in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When Tenghong fell in battle, Tenghe fought on through his tears, carried the victory to completion, and succeeded to command of the army.

sentences.zh: 進援臨江，复峽江。

translations.literal: He advanced to aid Linjiang and recovered Xiajiang.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to relieve Linjiang and recaptured Xiajiang.

sentences.zh: 會攻吉安，當西南路，掘長壕久困之。

translations.literal: Joining in the attack on Ji'an, he held the southwestern route, dug a long trench, and for a long time besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: In the joint assault on Ji'an he held the southwestern sector, digging a long trench to starve the garrison into submission.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，賊乘江漲突圍出，兩次皆擊退，尋拔其城。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year rebels took advantage of the river's rise to break out; twice they were beaten back; soon afterward the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eighth year the rebels exploited the flooded river to break out; twice they were repulsed, and the city was soon taken.

sentences.zh: 率所部窮追，斬馘過半。

translations.literal: Leading his own division he pursued to the end, beheading and killing more than half.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued relentlessly with his own troops, cutting down more than half the fleeing rebels.

sentences.zh: 調防九江，屯彭澤。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison Jiujiang and encamped at Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: Reassigned to defend Jiujiang, he encamped at Pengze.

sentences.zh: 九年二月，戰牯牛嶺，進攻建德風雲嶺賊巢，破其二壘。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year he fought at Guniu Ridge, advanced to attack the rebel nest at Fengyun Ridge in Jiande, and broke two of their forts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the ninth year he fought at Guniu Ridge and advanced on the rebel stronghold at Fengyun Ridge in Jiande, destroying two of their fortifications.

sentences.zh: 賊大至，被圍，力戰死之，年二十有八。

translations.literal: Rebels arrived in great numbers; surrounded, he fought fiercely and died; his age was twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: A large rebel force arrived and surrounded him. He fought to the death at the age of twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 官候選知府，詔依道員例賜卹，予騎都尉世職，附祀兄祠。

translations.literal: His office was expectant prefect; an edict granted funeral honors following the circuit-intendant pattern, awarded a hereditary captaincy, and enshrined him alongside his elder brother's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of expectant prefect. An edict granted him funeral honors at the rank of a circuit intendant, a hereditary captaincy, and a place in his brother's memorial shrine.

sentences.zh: =蔣益澧=蔣益澧，字薌泉，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: =Jiang Yili= Jiang Yili, styled Xiangquan, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yili, whose style was Xiangquan, came from Xiangxiang County in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 少不羈，不諧於鄉里，客遊四方。

translations.literal: In youth he was unrestrained, did not harmonize with the villagers, and traveled as a guest in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was wild and ill at ease in his home village, and wandered far and wide.

sentences.zh: 湖南軍事起，從王珍攻岳州，以功敘從九品。

translations.literal: When Hunan military affairs began, he followed Wang Zhen to attack Yuezhou and for merit was recorded at the rank of subordinate clerk of the ninth grade.
translations.idiomatic: When the military crisis erupted in Hunan, he joined Wang Zhen in the assault on Yuezhou and was appointed a ninth-rank clerk for his service.

sentences.zh: 复隸羅澤南部下，勇敢常先人，澤南異之，許列弟子籍。

translations.literal: Again he served under Luo Zeren's command; in courage he was often ahead of others; Zeren regarded him as exceptional and permitted him to be enrolled among the disciples.
translations.idiomatic: He later served under Luo Zeren, always leading the charge in battle. Zeren singled him out for his bravery and enrolled him among his disciples.

sentences.zh: 從克黃梅，擢縣丞。

translations.literal: Following in the capture of Huangmei, he was promoted to assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Huangmei and was promoted to assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 進剿九江，連敗賊於白水港、小池口。

translations.literal: Advancing to suppress Jiujiang, he repeatedly defeated rebels at Baishuigang and Xiaohekou.
translations.idiomatic: In the drive against Jiujiang he won successive victories over the rebels at Baishuigang and Xiaohekou.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，進攻廣信。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng he advanced to attack Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Xianfeng reign he marched on Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 大軍駐城西烏石山，益澧屯山右。

translations.literal: The main army encamped at Wushishan west of the city; Yili encamped on the mountain's right.
translations.idiomatic: The main force encamped at Wushi Mountain west of the city while Yili held the right flank of the hill.

sentences.zh: 賊覷其壘未成，來攻。

translations.literal: The rebels saw his fort was not yet complete and came to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that his fortifications were incomplete, the rebels attacked.

sentences.zh: 益澧堅壁不動，伺懈縱擊，斬賊首於陣。

translations.literal: Yili held fast within his walls without moving, waited for slackness and then released an attack, beheading a rebel chief in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yili held his position behind stout defenses until the enemy slackened, then sallied forth and killed a rebel chieftain in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 進逼城下，諸軍蟻附而登，復其城。

translations.literal: Advancing to press the city walls, the armies climbed like ants swarming up and recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing to the walls, the allied armies swarmed up like ants and recaptured the city.

sentences.zh: 進攻義寧，澤南潛師進鼇嶺，令益澧分駐乾坑。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Yining, Zeren secretly led troops forward to Aoling and ordered Yili to detach and encamp at Qiankeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the advance on Yining, Zeren secretly marched on Aoling while ordering Yili to hold Qiankeng with a detached force.

sentences.zh: 賊來爭，分數千人抄官軍後。

translations.literal: Rebels came to contest; they divided several thousand men to outflank the government army's rear.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came to dispute the position, detaching several thousand men to strike the imperial forces from the rear.

sentences.zh: 益澧曰：「今以數百人當大敵，不死戰，將殞。」

translations.literal: Yili said: "Now with several hundred men facing a great enemy, if we do not fight to the death, we will perish."
translations.idiomatic: Yili said, "With only a few hundred men against a massive enemy, if we do not fight to the death, we are finished."

sentences.zh: 揮兵直薄之，當者披靡，遂會師鼇嶺，乘勝复義寧，擢知縣。

translations.literal: He waved his troops straight to press close on them; all who met them were overthrown; then joined forces at Aoling, rode the victory to recover Yining, and was promoted to county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He charged straight at the enemy; none could stand before him. Joining Zeren at Aoling, they pressed their advantage and recaptured Yining, and Yili was promoted to county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 從澤南迴援武昌。

translations.literal: He followed Zeren to return and aid Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Zeren back to relieve Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 在軍與李續賓論事不相下，及澤南歿，續賓代將。

translations.literal: In the army he and Li Xubin debated affairs without yielding to each other; when Zeren died, Xubin took command in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: In camp he and Li Xubin quarreled as equals over military matters. After Zeren's death, Xubin succeeded to command.

sentences.zh: 益澧屯魯港，賊攻之急，請援，續賓置之。

translations.literal: Yili encamped at Lugang; rebels attacked fiercely; he requested aid; Xubin put it aside.
translations.idiomatic: Yili was encamped at Lugang when the rebels pressed him hard. He appealed for reinforcements, but Xubin ignored him.

sentences.zh: 益澧大恚，憑壘死守，賊旋引去。

translations.literal: Yili was greatly enraged; relying on his fort he defended to the death; the rebels soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Yili defended his fortifications to the last. The rebels soon withdrew of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 益澧遂告歸，不待報而行。

translations.literal: Yili then requested leave to return home and departed without waiting for a reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yili resigned and went home without waiting for approval.

sentences.zh: 嗣武漢克復，仍論前功，擢知府，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Subsequently when Wuhan was recovered, his earlier merits were still assessed; he was promoted to prefect and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuhan was recovered, his earlier service was recognized with promotion to prefect and the award of a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 益澧家居，悒悒不得志，會廣西匪熾，乞援於湖南，湖南宿將盡出征，駱秉章顧左右無可屬者，益澧請行，乃令率千六百人赴之。

translations.literal: Yili was at home, dejected and frustrated; just then Guangxi banditry was fierce; they begged aid from Hunan; Hunan's veteran generals had all gone out on campaign; Luo Bingzhang looked to left and right and there was no one to entrust; Yili requested to go; he was then ordered to lead sixteen hundred men to proceed there.
translations.idiomatic: Living at home in frustrated obscurity, he volunteered when Guangxi's bandit crisis deepened and Hunan was asked for aid. With every veteran general already in the field, Governor Luo Bingzhang could find no one else to command the relief force. Yili offered himself and was sent with sixteen hundred men.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，連破賊於賣珠嶺、唐家市，復興安、靈川；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year he repeatedly defeated rebels at Maizhu Ridge and Tangjia Market, and recovered Xing'an and Lingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year he routed the rebels at Maizhu Ridge and Tangjia Market and recovered Xing'an and Lingchuan.

sentences.zh: 艇匪踞平樂二塘墟、沙子街，進破之，焚賊艇，薄平樂，克之：擢道員，賜號額哲爾克巴圖魯，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: Boat bandits occupied Pingle's Ertang Market and Shazijie; advancing he broke them, burned rebel boats, pressed close on Pingle, and captured it: he was promoted to circuit intendant, granted the title Ezeker Batulu, and given the rank of surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Boat pirates held Ertang Market and Shazijie at Pingle. He attacked and broke them, burned their vessels, pressed on to Pingle and captured it. He was promoted to circuit intendant, granted the title Ezeker Batulu, and given the rank of surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 巡撫勞崇光疏請留於廣西補用，八年，入屯桂林。

translations.literal: Governor La Chongguang memorialized requesting that he be retained for appointment in Guangxi; in the eighth year he entered and encamped at Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Governor La Chongguang petitioned to keep him in Guangxi service. In the eighth year he entered the province and established headquarters at Guilin.

sentences.zh: 時廣西兵食並絀，率藉招撫馭盜，兵賊相糅，橫行無忌，疆吏不能制。

translations.literal: At that time Guangxi's military provisions and food were both short; they generally relied on recruitment-and-pacification to control bandits; soldiers and bandits mingled together, rampaging without restraint; border officials could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi at the time suffered from shortages of both troops and provisions. Bandits were kept in check only through a policy of enlistment and amnesty, soldiers and outlaws mingled freely, and they terrorized the countryside with impunity while provincial officials proved powerless to stop them.

sentences.zh: 益澧至，乘兵威，悉按誅桀黠者，易置守軍，人心始定。

translations.literal: When Yili arrived, riding military might he entirely according to law executed the most cunning and fierce, replaced the garrison troops, and people's hearts for the first time settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Yili arrived, he used military authority to execute the most notorious ringleaders, replaced the garrison troops, and only then did public order begin to return.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章奏助益澧軍月餉二萬，造船六十艘，募水師以益其軍。

translations.literal: Luo Bingzhang memorialized to assist Yili's army with twenty thousand taels monthly pay, build sixty boats, and recruit a river force to augment his army.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Bingzhang secured a monthly subsidy of twenty thousand taels for Yili's army, the construction of sixty boats, and the recruitment of a naval force to strengthen his command.

sentences.zh: 省城既固，進規右江。

translations.literal: Once the provincial capital was secure, he advanced to plan the Right River region.
translations.idiomatic: With the provincial capital secured, he turned his attention to the Right River region.

sentences.zh: 賊踞柳州，連結洞砦，恃水師不能至。

translations.literal: Rebels occupied Liuzhou, linked cave fortresses, and relied on the fact that the river force could not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held Liuzhou and a network of cave fortresses, confident that government forces could not reach them by water.

sentences.zh: 益澧具舟修仁，令軍士舁舢板陸行九十里，置洛青水中，載砲而下，遇賊洛垢墟，火賊舟。

translations.literal: Yili prepared boats at Xiuren, ordered soldiers to carry sampans overland ninety li, placed them in the Luqing water, loaded cannon and went downstream; encountering rebels at Luogou Market, they burned rebel boats.
translations.idiomatic: Yili had boats prepared at Xiuren and ordered his men to portage sampans overland for ninety li, launch them on the Luqing River with artillery aboard, and float downstream. At Luogou Market they set fire to the rebel boats.

sentences.zh: 次日，賊水陸並集，力戰斬賊數千，進鷓鴣山，攻柳州克之，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: The next day rebels gathered by land and water; fighting fiercely they beheaded several thousand rebels, advanced to Zhegu Mountain, attacked and captured Liuzhou, and he was given the rank of administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels massed by land and water. After fierce fighting in which thousands were slain, he advanced to Zhegu Mountain, stormed Liuzhou, and was granted the rank of administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 偕右江道張凱嵩會剿慶遠，掘長壕斷賊出入，賊渡河竄，邀擊敗之。

translations.literal: Together with Right River Circuit Zhang Kaisong he jointly suppressed Qingyuan, dug a long trench to cut off rebel ingress and egress; rebels crossed the river and fled; they intercepted and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Zhang Kaisong, the Right River intendant, he jointly suppressed Qingyuan, digging a long trench to block rebel movement. When the rebels fled across the river, he intercepted and routed them.

sentences.zh: 慶遠平，以按察使記名。

translations.literal: Qingyuan was pacified; he was put on the register as surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: With Qingyuan pacified, he was registered for appointment as surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九年，石達開竄湖南，前隊掠全州，益澧分兵守柳州，自回援省城，授按察使，尋遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Shi Dakai fled into Hunan; the vanguard plundered Quanzhou; Yili divided troops to guard Liuzhou and personally returned to aid the provincial capital; he was appointed surveillance commissioner and soon transferred to administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Shi Dakai fled into Hunan and his vanguard raided Quanzhou. Yili detached troops to hold Liuzhou and returned personally to relieve the provincial capital. He was appointed surveillance commissioner and soon promoted to administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 出剿恭城土匪，扼平樂。

translations.literal: He went out to suppress Gongcheng bandits and held Pingle in check.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against bandits in Gongcheng and secured Pingle.

sentences.zh: 粵匪石國宗由全州、興安窺桂林，勢甚張。

translations.literal: Cantonese bandits under Shi Guozong from Quanzhou and Xing'an eyed Guilin; their momentum was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese rebels under Shi Guozong, advancing from Quanzhou and Xing'an, threatened Guilin with formidable strength.

sentences.zh: 學政李載熙劾益澧失機及冒餉忌功等事，詔念益澧前勞，降道員，留廣西，並下疆臣察奏。

translations.literal: Education intendant Li Zaixi impeached Yili for missing opportunities and for embezzling pay, envying merit, and the like; an edict remembering Yili's earlier labors demoted him to circuit intendant, retained him in Guangxi, and also sent down orders to border officials to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: Education Intendant Li Zaixi impeached Yili for missing opportunities, padding payrolls, and resenting others' achievements. The throne, mindful of his earlier service, demoted him to circuit intendant but kept him in Guangxi and ordered a provincial investigation.

sentences.zh: 會湖南遣劉長佑、蕭啟江率師來援，益澧與合剿，解桂林圍。

translations.literal: Just then Hunan sent Liu Changyou and Xiao Qijiang leading armies to aid; Yili joined them in joint suppression and relieved the siege of Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan then dispatched Liu Changyou and Xiao Qijiang with relief armies. Yili joined them in a joint campaign that lifted the siege of Guilin.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章、曹澍鍾並為疏辨，得白。

translations.literal: Luo Bingzhang and Cao Shuzhong both submitted memorials in his defense; he was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Bingzhang and Cao Shuzhong both submitted memorials in his defense, and he was exonerated.

sentences.zh: 十年，賀縣匪分擾昭平、平樂，益澧擊走之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year He County bandits separately harassed Zhaoping and Pingle; Yili attacked and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year bandits from He County raided Zhaoping and Pingle; Yili drove them off.

sentences.zh: 進破賊首陳金剛於大灣嶺，焚沙田賊寨，复布政使原銜。

translations.literal: Advancing he broke the rebel chief Chen Jingang at Dawanshan, burned the bandit stockade at Shatian, and restored his original rank of administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the rebel chief Chen Jingang at Dawanshan, burned the stockade at Shatian, and was restored to his former rank of administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又會廣東援師破賊於竹洞嶺。

translations.literal: Again he joined Guangdong relief troops to defeat rebels at Zhudong Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Guangdong relief forces to defeat the rebels at Zhudong Ridge.

sentences.zh: 十一年，复授廣西按察使，進駐平南。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was again appointed Guangxi surveillance commissioner and advanced to encamp at Pingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was reappointed Guangxi surveillance commissioner and advanced his headquarters to Pingnan.

sentences.zh: 偕總兵李揚升复潯州，复布政使原官。

translations.literal: Together with Regional Commander Li Yangsheng he recovered Xunzhou and restored his original post of administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Regional Commander Li Yangsheng he recaptured Xunzhou and was restored to his former post of administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 益澧年少戇急，曾國籓、胡林翼素不滿之，而左宗棠特器重。

translations.literal: Yili was young, rash, and impetuous; Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi had never been satisfied with him, but Zuo Zongtang especially valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Young, blunt, and hot-tempered, Yili had never pleased Zeng Guofan or Hu Linyi, but Zuo Zongtang held him in special esteem.

sentences.zh: 至是宗棠規浙江，疏請以益澧為助。

translations.literal: At this time Zongtang was planning Zhejiang and memorialized requesting Yili as assistance.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuo turned his attention to Zhejiang, he petitioned for Yili to join him.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，調浙江布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was transferred to administration commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign he was appointed administration commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 自湖南增募八千人，道廣東，總督勞崇光資以餉械。

translations.literal: From Hunan he raised an additional eight thousand men, passed through Guangdong; Governor La Chongguang supplied him with pay and arms.
translations.idiomatic: He raised an additional eight thousand men in Hunan, marched through Guangdong, and Governor La Chongguang furnished him with funds and weapons.

sentences.zh: 九月，至衢州，分兵复壽昌。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he reached Quzhou and divided troops to recover Shouchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he reached Quzhou and detached troops to recapture Shouchang.

sentences.zh: 賊酋李世賢屯裘家堰，按察使劉典兵先進，益澧繼之，降賊李世詳為內應，襲破之，悉毀賊壘。

translations.literal: Rebel chieftain Li Shixian encamped at Qiujia Dam; Surveillance Commissioner Liu Dian's troops advanced first, Yili followed; rebel Li Shixiang defected as an inside collaborator; they made a surprise attack and broke them, entirely destroying the rebel forts.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chief Li Shixian held Qiujia Dam. Surveillance Commissioner Liu Dian's force led the attack with Yili following. Li Shixiang, a rebel defector, served as inside collaborator, and in a surprise assault they smashed the position and destroyed all the fortifications.

sentences.zh: 二年，克湯溪，被珍賚優敘。

translations.literal: In the second year Tangxi was captured; he received precious gifts and preferential commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Tangxi fell, and he received imperial gifts and special commendation.

sentences.zh: 宗棠進屯嚴州，規富陽，援賊麕至，益澧渡江築壘新橋，分三路迎擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Zongtang advanced to encamp at Yanzhou, planned Fuyang; relief rebels gathered thickly; Yili crossed the river and built forts at Xinqiao, divided three routes to meet and attack, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo advanced to Yanzhou to prepare an assault on Fuyang. Rebel reinforcements massed in force. Yili crossed the river, fortified Xinqiao, and engaged them on three fronts, routing them completely.

sentences.zh: 會游擊徐文秀等攻雞籠山，益澧自督戰，盡破十餘壘。

translations.literal: Just then Brigadier Xu Wenxiu and others attacked Jilong Mountain; Yili personally supervised the battle and entirely broke more than ten forts.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Brigadier Xu Wenxiu and others assaulted Jilong Mountain. Yili personally directed the fighting and destroyed more than ten rebel fortifications.

sentences.zh: 八月，克富陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Fuyang was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Fuyang fell.

sentences.zh: 自杭州至餘杭，賊營連數十里。

translations.literal: From Hangzhou to Yuhang, rebel camps stretched in succession for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: From Hangzhou to Yuhang, rebel encampments lined the route for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 益澧沿江下逼清波、鳳山兩門，據十里街、六和塔、萬松嶺，俯瞰城中，自駐東嶽廟，賊屢出犯，皆擊退。

translations.literal: Yili pressed down along the river to threaten the Qingbo and Fengshan gates, seized Shili Street, Liuhe Pagoda, and Wansong Ridge, overlooking the city from above; he personally encamped at the Dongyue Temple; rebels repeatedly came out to attack and all were beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: Yili pressed downriver toward the Qingbo and Fengshan gates, seizing Shili Street, Liuhe Pagoda, and Wansong Ridge to overlook the city from the heights. He established his headquarters at the Dongyue Temple, and repeated rebel sorties were driven back.

sentences.zh: 分兵會道員楊昌濬、總兵黃少春攻餘杭，敗賊城下，匿不出。

translations.literal: He divided troops to join Circuit Intendant Yang Changjun and Regional Commander Huang Shaochun in attacking Yuhang, defeated rebels beneath the walls, and they hid and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: He detached troops to join Circuit Intendant Yang Changjun and Regional Commander Huang Shaochun in the assault on Yuhang, routed the rebels at the walls, and they withdrew into the city and refused to emerge.

sentences.zh: 又破鳳山門、清泰門賊壘，由錢江入西湖，奪賊舟。

translations.literal: He again broke the rebel ramparts at Fengshan Gate and Qingtai Gate, entered West Lake by the Qiantang River, and seized rebel boats.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed the forts at Fengshan and Qingtai gates, entered West Lake by the Qiantang River, and captured the enemy fleet.

sentences.zh: 平湖、乍浦、海鹽皆下，海寧守賊蔡元吉、桐鄉守賊何紹章先後投誠效用。

translations.literal: Pinghu, Zhapu, and Haiyan all fell; the defending rebels at Haining, Cai Yuanji, and at Tongxiang, He Shaozhang, successively submitted and offered their service.
translations.idiomatic: Pinghu, Zhapu, and Haiyan fell; the Haining garrison commander Cai Yuanji and the Tongxiang commander He Shaozhang surrendered in turn and entered Qing service.

sentences.zh: 三年，令紹章扼烏鎮，元吉會蘇師复嘉興，賊勢日蹙。

translations.literal: In the third year he ordered Shaozhang to hold Wuzhen; Yuanji joined the Jiangsu army in recovering Jiaxing, and the rebels' position grew daily more desperate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he posted Shaozhang at Wuzhen while Yuanji joined the Jiangsu forces in retaking Jiaxing; the rebel position tightened by the day.

sentences.zh: 二月，饅頭山地雷發，壞城垣，諸軍擁入，戰竟日，悍賊多斃，餘夜遁，遂復杭州，餘杭亦下。

translations.literal: In the second month the land mine at Mantou Hill exploded, destroyed the wall, the various armies surged in, fought all day, many fierce rebels were killed, the remainder fled by night, and thereby Hangzhou was recovered and Yuhang also fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month a mine at Mantou Hill breached the wall; the armies poured in and fought all day. Most of the hard core were killed and the rest fled by night; Hangzhou was retaken and Yuhang fell as well.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其功，賜黃馬褂，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: An edict praised his merit, granted the yellow riding jacket, and gave the hereditary office of Cloud Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his service, awarded the yellow riding jacket, and granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 分軍克德清、石門，進攻湖州。

translations.literal: He detached troops to capture Deqing and Shimen and advanced to attack Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He detached columns to take Deqing and Shimen and pressed the attack on Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 蔡元吉深入，為賊所圍，益澧自往援之。

translations.literal: Cai Yuanji penetrated deep and was surrounded by rebels; Yili went in person to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yuanji pushed deep and was surrounded; Yili went to relieve him in person.

sentences.zh: 轉戰而前，距元吉營隔一河未達。

translations.literal: Fighting as he advanced, he was separated from Yuanji's camp by a river and did not reach it.
translations.idiomatic: He fought his way forward but was stopped a river short of Yuanji's camp.

sentences.zh: 時偽幼王洪福瑱遁入湖州，悍酋黃文金眾尚十餘萬。

translations.literal: At this time the false Young King Hong Fuzhen had fled into Huzhou, and the fierce chieftain Huang Wenjin still had a force of more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping Young King Hong Fuzhen had fled into Huzhou, and the fierce commander Huang Wenjin still commanded more than a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 七月，作浮橋通元吉營，出湖趺漾襲賊後。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he built a pontoon bridge to reach Yuanji's camp, went out from Hudieyang Lake, and struck the rebels in the rear.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he bridged the river to Yuanji's camp, sortied from Hudieyang Lake, and hit the enemy from the rear.

sentences.zh: 降賊譚侍友出太湖攻袁家匯，賊棄城走，邀擊之，解散數万人。

translations.literal: The surrendered rebel Tan Shiyou went out from Taihu Lake to attack Yuanjia Hui; the rebels abandoned the city and fled; he intercepted them and disbanded several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The defector Tan Shiyou attacked Yuanjia Hui from Taihu Lake; the rebels abandoned the city and fled, were intercepted, and tens of thousands were dispersed.

sentences.zh: 浙境肅清，晉騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: Zhejiang territory was pacified; he was advanced to hereditary Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhejiang pacified he was promoted to hereditary Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠追賊赴福建，益澧護理巡撫。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang pursued the rebels to Fujian, and Yili acted as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuo Zongtang pursued the rebels into Fujian, Yili served as acting governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 疏陳善後事宜，籌閩餉，濬湖汊，築海塘，捕槍匪，又覈減漕糧，酌裁關稅，商農相率來歸。

translations.literal: He memorialized on measures of postwar settlement, raised funds for Fujian, dredged lake channels, built sea dikes, captured gun-running bandits, also verified and reduced grain transport taxes, adjusted customs duties as appropriate, and merchants and farmers came back in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on reconstruction: raised funds for Fujian, dredged lake channels, built sea walls, suppressed gun-runners, cut transport taxes and customs levies, and merchants and farmers returned in numbers.

sentences.zh: 增書院膏火，建經生講舍，設義學，興善堂，百廢具舉。

translations.literal: He increased stipends for academy students, built lecture halls for classicists, established charity schools and halls of benevolence, and a hundred neglected tasks were all undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: He increased academy stipends, built lecture halls, founded charity schools and benevolent halls, and revived a hundred neglected institutions.

sentences.zh: 東南諸省善後之政，以浙江為最。

translations.literal: Among the southeastern provinces' policies of postwar settlement, Zhejiang's were foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the southeastern provinces' reconstruction programs, Zhejiang's ranked first.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，乃回本任。

translations.literal: After more than a year he then returned to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he returned to his regular post.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢廣東巡撫，奏裁太平關稅陋規四萬兩，斥革丁胥，改由巡撫委員徵收；

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to governor of Guangdong, memorialized to abolish corrupt customs practices at Taiping Pass amounting to forty thousand taels, dismissed clerks and runners, and changed to collection by commissioners appointed by the governor;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he became governor of Guangdong, abolished forty thousand taels of corrupt levies at Taiping Pass customs, dismissed abusive clerks, and put collection under commissioners appointed by the governor;

sentences.zh: 五坑客匪投誠，分別安插高、廣各府，另編客籍；

translations.literal: Hakka bandits of Wukeng submitted, were separately resettled in the prefectures of Gaozhou and Guangzhou, and given a separate guest registration;
translations.idiomatic: Hakka bandits of Wukeng surrendered and were resettled across the Gaozhou and Guangzhou prefectures under a separate guest register;

sentences.zh: 設學額：並如議行。

translations.literal: Established examination quotas: all were carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: and established examination quotas, all as proposed.

sentences.zh: 六年，以病乞休。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he requested retirement on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋為總督瑞麟疏劾，下閩浙總督吳棠按奏，坐任性不依例案，部議降四級，改降二級，以按察使候補，命赴左宗棠軍營差委。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Governor-General Ruilin memorialized in impeachment; the case was sent to Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Wu Tang for investigation and report; he was found guilty of willfulness and disregard of precedent, the Board proposed demotion by four ranks, changed to demotion by two ranks, to await appointment as provincial surveillance commissioner, and was ordered to go to Zuo Zongtang's camp for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Governor-General Ruilin impeached him; Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Wu Tang investigated and found him guilty of willful disregard of regulations. The Board proposed a four-rank demotion, reduced to two; he was to await appointment as surveillance commissioner and was ordered to Zuo Zongtang's camp for assignment.

sentences.zh: 尋授廣西按察使，以病回籍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed provincial surveillance commissioner of Guangxi and returned to his native place on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made surveillance commissioner of Guangxi but returned home on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 十三年，日本窺臺灣，召至京。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Japan cast covetous eyes on Taiwan; he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when Japan threatened Taiwan, he was summoned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 未及任用，病卒。

translations.literal: Before he could be appointed he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness before any new appointment could be made.

sentences.zh: 太常寺卿周瑞清疏陳益澧廣西政績，詔復原官，依巡撫例賜卹。

translations.literal: Grand Master of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhou Ruiqing memorialized on Yili's administrative achievements in Guangxi; an edict restored his former rank and granted posthumous gifts according to the precedent for governors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ruiqing of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized on Yili's record in Guangxi; the court restored his former rank and granted posthumous honors on the governor's precedent.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡撫楊昌濬、梅啟照先後疏言平浙功尤鉅，詔允建祠，諡果敏。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Governors Yang Changjun and Mei Qizhao successively memorialized that his merit in pacifying Zhejiang was especially great; an edict permitted the building of a shrine and gave the posthumous title Guomin.
translations.idiomatic: Governors Yang Changjun and Mei Qizhao both stressed his outstanding role in pacifying Zhejiang; the court authorized a temple and gave him the posthumous name Guomin, Resolute and Keen.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：李續賓果毅仁廉，治軍一守羅澤南遺法，戡定武昌、九江，戰績為一時之冠。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Li Xubin was resolute, benevolent, and incorruptible; in governing the army he wholly kept Luo Zeren's legacy methods; he pacified Wuchang and Jiujiang, and his battle achievements were the crown of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Li Xubin was resolute, humane, and incorruptible. He ran his army strictly by Luo Zeren's methods, pacified Wuchang and Jiujiang, and for a time his record of battle stood above all others.

sentences.zh: 李續宜獨以持重稱，殆鑑於其兄之銳進不終而然耶？

translations.literal: Li Xuyi alone was famed for steadiness—was this perhaps because he took warning from his elder brother's sharp advance without a peaceful end?
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuyi alone was known for caution—perhaps he had learned from his brother's daring advance and tragic end.

sentences.zh: 王珍、劉騰鴻皆出奇制勝，駿利無敵，惜早殞，未竟其功。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen and Liu Tenghong both won by surprise tactics, were swift and invincible, but alas died young and did not complete their merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen and Liu Tenghong both won by surprise and seemed invincible in their prime, but died young and left their work unfinished.

sentences.zh: 蔣益澧經挫折而奮起，平浙、治浙，並著顯績，信乎能自樹立。

translations.literal: Jiang Yili, after setbacks, roused himself; in pacifying Zhejiang and governing Zhejiang he alike showed distinguished achievement—truly he could establish himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yili rose again after setbacks, pacified Zhejiang and governed it to lasting effect—truly a man who made his own standing.

sentences.zh: 諸人並湘軍之傑，不以名位論高下也。

translations.literal: All these men were outstanding figures of the Hunan Army; one does not rank them high or low by name and position.
translations.idiomatic: All were eminent men of the Hunan Army, and their worth is not to be measured by rank alone.
